DEADLINES 
Fall semester:  
Nomination deadline: May 15th for non-EU students, June 1st for EU students 
Application deadline: June 1st for non-EU students, June 15th for EU students 
 
Spring semester:  
Nomination deadline: October 15th  
Application deadline: October 31st 
 
 
NOMINATION PROCESS 
Universities have received an Excel file to fill out with the information of the students they 
wish to nominate. This nomination file is to be sent per email to ri@ensea.fr. Please 
contact ri@ensea.fr if you need to receive the new Excel template.  
 
 
LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS 
French: B1 certificate   English: B2 certificate 
 
We offer English-taught courses at Master level (2nd and 3rd year at ENSEA). 
Available courses can be found here. Details available upon request at ri@ensea.fr  
If students are following English-taught courses only, they do not have to show proof of a 
certain level of French. However they will participate in mandatory French language 
class during their entire stay at ENSEA.  
Although some courses are held in English, and student can follow their entire study in 
English, our language of instruction is mainly French. To have a successful exchange 
experience in France, we recommend students to prepare their language skills 
before they come to Cergy. 
 
 
ACADEMIC CALENDAR 
Fall semester: September to mid-January (retake exams mid-March, possible online) 
Spring semester: January to mid-April + internship until August if required 
 
 
VISA REQUIREMENTS 
 
Non-EU citizens must obtain a visa to study in France. Students must apply for a “long-stay 
student visa (VLS-TS)” on the France Visa website. 
Students shall anticipate their application! The length of the procedure may vary 
depending on the country of origin, but it generally takes several weeks. Beware of delays 
during busy periods, particularly from July to September. 
ENSEA International Office will guide incoming students through that process. 
 
 
ACCOMMODATION 
 
Student accommodation prices in Cergy vary between 300€ and 800€ per month.  
Every year, ENSEA can accommodate most incoming students in nearby student residences. 
However please be aware that places are limited and subject to the “first come first 
serve” rule. Priority is given to students coming to France for the first time.  

【第3頁】
 
 
 
 
ÉCOLE NATIONALE SUP ÉRIEURE DE L’ ÉLECTRONIQUE ET DE SES APPLICATIONS  
6, avenue du Ponceau • CS20707 Cergy • 95014 Cergy-Pontoise Cedex • France 
01 30 73 66 66 • www.ensea.fr 
To find private accommodation in Cergy, please find useful information on our website.  
 
Governmental update: Starting in July 2026, non-European students will not have 
access to financial housing benefits from the French government anymore. We 
advise all students to take this into consideration when planning their budget for France.  
 
 
STUDENTS WITH SPECIAL NEEDS 
 
ENSEA and its community are committed to combating all forms of discrimination, even 
implicit, and are committed to a comprehensive approach to welcoming diversity 
among its students and staff. If your students require any type of specific support, please 
inform us in advance so we can adapt and prepare the best conditions for them. More 
information on our website.  
 
 
BIENVENUE EN FRANCE LABEL 
 
ENSEA has been one of the first winners to benefit from the 
Bienvenue en France label as well as the Campus France seed fund since 
its creation in 2019. In 2024, the school is proud to have obtained the 
3-star Bienvenue en France level, the highest level of 
certification. This distinction demonstrates the exceptional quality of the 
welcome and support provided to its international students from all over the 
world.  
We look forward to receiving your students at ENSEA!  
See you soon in Cergy!

Home

FAME Program
Share:
FAME, short for “French American Exchange Program”, is an international exchange program created in 2008 between ENSEA and prestigious American universities: the Illinois Institute of Technology and the University at Buffalo. Since then, several institutions have joined the agreement and send us students each year for a spring semester at one of the top French engineering schools.
The FAME program is for students in their third year of an ABET-accredited undergraduate program with a major in electrical engineering or computer science.
FAME's goal is to introduce American students to our high-quality education through courses taught in English for a semester. Credits earned during this semester are transferable.
The FAME program takes place every year between mid-January and the end of May (15 weeks of classes and 2 x 2-week breaks).

ACTIVER MON ESPACE PERSONNEL
Le lien vers cette page a été envoyé avec succès aux destinataires.
Un étudiant peut-il bénéficier d'une aide au logement (APL, ALS, ALF) pour payer son loyer ?
Vérifié le 01 juillet 2026 - Service Public / Direction de l'information légale et administrative (Premier ministre)
Oui,
un étudiant peut bénéficier sous conditions d'une aide au logement pour l'aider à payer son loyer.
Il existe
3 types d'aides
au logement :
Aide personnalisée au logement (APL)
Allocation de logement familiale (ALF)
Allocation de logement sociale (ALS)
.
Vous pouvez bénéficier de
l'une de ces 3 aides
si vous respectez les
4 conditions suivantes
:
Vous êtes français, ou étranger avec un
titre de séjour
en cours de validité
Vous louez un
logement décent
Vous n'avez pas
de lien de parenté avec le propriétaire du logement
Vous avez de faibles ressources.
Depuis le 1
er
juillet 2026
, si vous êtes étudiant ressortissant d'un pays hors
Union européenne (UE)
: titleContent
,
Espace économique européen (EEE)
: titleContent
ou Suisse et possédez un titre de séjour délivré pour les études, vous pouvez bénéficier d’une aide au logement uniquement dans l'un des 3 cas suivants :
Vous percevez une
bourse sur critères sociaux
(du centre régional des œuvres universitaires et scolaires - Crous, ou une bourse régionale sanitaire et sociale alignée sur les critères sociaux)
Vous exercez une activité professionnelle
Vous êtes engagé dans un
contrat d’apprentissage ou de professionnalisation
.
Vous pouvez utiliser un simulateur pour avoir une estimation du montant de l'aide au logement auquel vous pouvez prétendre :
Calculer son droit à une aide personnelle au logement (APL, ALF, ALS) - Caf
Attention
Si vos parents perçoivent des allocations familiales et que vous demandez une aide au logement, vous n'êtes plus considéré à la
charge de vos parents au sens des prestations familiales
. Leurs allocations peuvent diminuer, voire être supprimées. Vous devez donc
choisir entre bénéficier d'une aide au logement ou rester à la charge de vos parents
.
Votre demande d'aide au logement doit être faite en ligne :
Aide au logement étudiant : demande en ligne
Il est recommandé de faire votre demande d'aide au logement dès l'installation dans votre logement.
En cas de
colocation
, chaque colocataire peut bénéficier d'une aide au logement. Il faut alors que chacun fasse sa propre demande à son nom. Le calcul de l'aide au logement prend en compte la part de loyer versée par chacun.
À savoir
Pour plus d'informations, vous pouvez appeler le numéro dédié aux aides au logement étudiant.
Où s’adresser ?
Aide au logement étudiant (APL, ALF, ALS)
Permet aux étudiants d'obtenir des informations sur les aides au logement (APL, ALS, ALF).
Par téléphone
09 69 32 52 52
Ouvert du lundi au vendredi de 9h à 16h30.
Prix d'un appel local depuis un téléphone fixe. Surcoût éventuel depuis un mobile selon les opérateurs.
Le 1
er
paiement de l'aide au logement est généralement effectué
2 mois après la demande
.
Exemple :
Si la demande est faite en février, votre droit est ouvert en mars et le 1
er
paiement s'effectue début avril.
À noter
La
garantie Visale
,
l'avance Loca-Pass
(aides pour accéder à un logement) et
l'aide Mobili-Jeune
(aide pour payer son loyer) sont cumulables avec l'APL, l'ALF ou l'ALS,
à condition de respecter les critères d'attribution de chaque dispositif
.

De Vinci Higher Education is made up of three schools that award accredited degrees: EMLV (Business School), ESILV (Engineering School) and IIM (School of Digital Communication). Exchange students from our partner universities can access our exchange programs in business and management at EMLV, and engineering at ESILV.
Business & Management – EMLV
EMLV Graduate School of Management is organized according to a 3+2 structure with 3 years of Undergraduate studies followed by a 2-year Graduate programme.
Students obtain a state accredited Master degree upon completion of 300 ECTS credits (5 years). Courses are taught in French or in English and are available
here
.
Exchange students have access to all courses provided they have a B2 level in the relevant language of instruction.
At Undergraduate level (year 1, 2 & 3):
On year 1 and 2, courses are taught in English and French, so exchange students should provide a B2 level certification in English & French
Year 3 is taught entirely in English, so only a B2 English level is necessary. On year 3, the same courses are taught in English during the first and the second semester. Exchange students are welcome to choose one of the semester.
At Graduate level (year 4 & 5/Master level), all courses are taught in English, so only a B2 English level is necessary. Students can choose between the following majors:
Master in Management – Corporate Finance
Master in Management – Audit & Performance Management
Master in Management – Financial Markets
Master in Management – Marketing & Communication
Master in Management – International Business
Please note :
It is not possible to pick up courses from various semesters, from various years nor majors. Exchange students must follow the courses of their chosen year and, at graduate/master level, of their chosen major.
Class attendance is mandatory.
Exchange students are required to follow 30 ECTS credits per semester

Students obtain a state accredited Master degree (Titre d’Ingénieur) upon completion of 300 ECTS credits (5 years). Courses are taught in French or in English and are available
here.

About Devinci Higher Education
Devinci Higher Education is a state-recognized, private higher education institution founded in 1995. It is made up of three schools that award accredited degrees: EMLV (Business School), ESILV (Engineering School) and IIM (School of Digital Communication & Multimedia).
A note on names: Devinci Higher Education, Léonard de Vinci group and Pôle Léonard de Vinci are used interchangeably to refer to the collective institution as composed of its three schools: EMLV, ESILV, and IIM.
De Vinci Higher Education encourages international openness and has developed numerous partnerships with foreign universities. The development of these partnerships has resulted in thousands of academic exchanges that have allowed French students to study in partner universities and foreign students to study at Pôle Léonard de Vinci schools.

Procedures and documents
Exchange students
Devinci Higher Education accepts only nominated students from partner institutions. If you are interested in coming for an exchange at Devinci Higher Education,
please contact your home institution.
Selection procedure: Nomination & registration
The selection process can be divided into different steps: nomination by your home institution, online registration and acceptance at Léonard de Vinci. Once accepted at Léonard de Vinci, you will receive an official acceptance letter, and later on login details to allow you to access the intranet.
We have two selection processes every academic year, one for the fall semester (first semester, August-December) and one for the spring semester (second semester, January-May). The specific deadline for nomination and registration will be communicated at the start of every academic year.
Applying for an exchange for the fall semester
Nomination process: April – mid-May
Online registration deadline: 1st June
Applying for an exchange for the spring semester
Nomination process: September-Mid October
Online registration deadline: 1st November
Documents to provide on registration (digital copies)
Identity photo (picture following the requirements of a passport picture)
Copy of identity document (ID or passport)
Copy of European health insurance card (for European students)
Proof of English Language Proficiency: (to be filled in by an English teacher, can be sent after registration).
Previous transcripts of records: for 4th and 5th year only (master/postgraduate level)! These can be sent after registration.
Support for exchange students
The Incoming Team of the International Relations Office is here to assist you during the registration process and during your installation in France. They will be there to guide you through information sessions before your exchange and orientation sessions on your arrival. During your exchange, they remain available: you can visit their office or reach them by email/phone for any questions you may have.
Important information
Academic Calendar
The specific dates will depend on the chosen school and program, but as a general guideline:
Fall semester: End August – third week of December
Spring semester: Early January – mid-May
Language of instruction
French or English: The language of instruction for each school and year is specified in the
Exchange programmes page
.
All exchange students will, as part of their program, follow French classes adapted to their level, even if you are complete beginner! This level will be determined via a non-graded test at the beginning of the exchange.
Housing
Devinci Higher Education does not provide its own accommodation, but has an own online platform called Studapart Devinci which concentrates safe and trustworthy adds for accommodation provided by private landlords. Around 60% of all our international students find their accommodation through Studapart Devinci.
More info and tips on how to find an accommodation In Paris will be given during the pre-mobility information sessions!

Incoming Exchange students
Incoming Exchange students
Every year, Rennes School of Business warmly welcomes incoming exchange students from its wide network of partner institutions. Whether you are coming for one semester or a full academic year, our exchange programmes offer a unique opportunity to study abroad in a vibrant campus environment.
Located in the heart of Rennes or Paris, our university campuses combines tradition, modern facilities, and a strong sense of community to ensure students thrive academically and socially. Our programmes are designed to provide an
international education
experience, fostering
global engagement
, personal growth, and professional development.
Joining our
exchange programmes
allows
university students
to learn and live in a dynamic French city, benefit from
academic advising
, and participate in
cultural exchange
activities that enhance their overall experience. With support services ranging from
campus housing
to
health insurance
, we aim to make your stay comfortable and enriching.
Programme objectives
By participating in our
incoming exchange student
programme, you will be able to:
Gain access to a high-quality
academic catalogue
in English, tailored to your
home institution
requirements
Engage with a diverse international student body, developing intercultural competence and global perspectives
Explore the city and immerse yourself in French culture while benefiting from on-campus and off-campus accommodation
Enhance your academic profile by earning credits transferable to your degree at your
home university
Receive support and guidance from dedicated coordinators throughout the
application process
and your
academic year
Experience a safe, inclusive, and vibrant campus, fostering both academic excellence and personal growth
Programme overview
Our
exchange programmes
, offered in English and tailored to different study levels, allow students to integrate easily into our
academic catalogue
. They are organised by
semester
.
Exchange – Level 2:
Second-year undergraduate students attend classes in the Bachelor in Management (BiM) programme, exclusively available during the
fall semester
. The cohort is highly international and multicultural
Exchange – Level 3:
Third-year students follow the final year of the BiM programme and choose a major in sales and marketing, finance and banking, or purchasing and supply chain management. Classes are taught in English
Exchange – Level 4:
First-year Master in Management modules are available alongside courses dedicated solely to
incoming exchange students
, offering a wide choice of credit-bearing courses in English
Exchange – Level 5:
Students attend modules from the second year of the Master in Management, including general management courses and specialise in a specific track, integrated with local students completing their final year
Conditions of admission
To be eligible for the programme, your
home university
must hold an
exchange agreement
with Rennes School of Business. You must also be a degree-seeking student at your
home institution
. Tuition is paid only to your
home university
, not RSB.
For further details on how and when to go abroad, and which programmes or subjects you should study, please ask the exchange coordinator at your home institution
You can come to RSB for one semester or for a full academic year (except level 2 – fall semester only)
You can earn credits to transfer towards your university degree at your home institution
Nomination and application
The first step to joining our
incoming exchange student
programme is the nomination by your
home university
. Once nominated, you will receive information to complete the
application process
. Required documents include:
Completed
application form
and
home university
coordinator form. Applicants must submit the completed forms before the stated deadline to ensure eligibility.
English language proficiency
proof (TOEFL/IELTS/TOEIC) or certificate from
home institution
. Meeting the
minimum score
requirement is essential for acceptance into the programme.
Copy of passport and passport-sized photo
Official
transcripts
from your
home university
CV in English
After review, a formal Letter of Acceptance will be sent, allowing you to start preparing for visa arrangements (if applicable),
campus housing
, and travel. The letter will include a link to essential resources and contacts for the term and class schedules.
Visa and immigration
Non-European students must contact the French Embassy or Campus France to obtain a
student visa
. Our
office of international
assists with guidance to ensure your
visa status
and
student and exchange visitor
documentation are correctly processed. Eligibility requirements may vary depending on the country of origin and the type of visa requested.
Orientation and academic year start
The school provides orientation days before classes begin, covering
academic advising, health insurance
, banking, mobile services, transport, and information on French culture. Participation is mandatory to ensure a smooth transition into both academic and social life on campus. Students are encouraged to visit the organisation’s orientation centre and contact staff for any questions during these hours.
Course registration
Once enrolled, students select courses through our online
course registration
platform. Learning agreements should be approved in consultation with your
home institution
. Credits earned are transferable, and academic transcripts are issued digitally at the end of the semester. Each subject carries a set number of hours and value, ensuring a balanced and comprehensive
academic year
schedule.
Accommodation
Rennes School of Business provides assistance in finding on-campus and off-campus accommodation, including student residences, shared flats, family homestays, and private houses, ensuring a safe and comfortable living environment. Students studying on-campus can enjoy convenient access to all college facilities and the campus center.
Exams and transcripts
Examinations take place at the end of each semester (December and April), with resit exams scheduled in June/July. Note that it is not possible to change exam dates upon the request of individual students.
Grading follows a clear system:
A – Excellent: 70%+
B – Very good: 65–69%
C – Good: 58–64%
D – Satisfactory: 50–57%
E – Sufficient: 40–49%
F/Fx – Fail: below 40%
Transcripts issuance is digital via the students’ platform.
Additional Services
RSB welcomes students with disabilities, providing lifts, adapted transport, and tailored support services. Please contact the school before arrival to inform us of any required assistance (by sending an email to the team in charge of the administration of your programme). Transport in Rennes is also adapted to persons with reduced mobility (metro & buses). The
internal Aloha platform
offers detailed resources on accommodation, healthcare, banking, and campus life.
FAQ – Incoming exchange students
How do I apply for the exchange programme?
Your home university nominates you online, after which you complete the application form and upload required documents.
Can I come for one semester only?
Yes, students can join for one semester or a full academic year, depending on the programme level.
What support is provided for accommodation?
RSB helps students find on-campus or off-campus housing, including student residences, shared flats, or family homestays.
Are classes taught in English?
Yes, all exchange programme courses are taught in English, ensuring smooth integration for international students.
How can I transfer credits to my home university?
Credits earned during your incoming exchange students semester are transferable with approval from your home institution. Academic advising ensures courses meet degree requirements.
Is Rennes a friendly city for students?
Regularly ranked as one of the youngest and most vibrant student cities in France, Rennes welcomes around 70,000 students every year. Locals love to mingle with them in one of the city’s many bars, restaurants and clubs.
Is it easy to travel from Rennes to other places in France?
Rennes is well connected via both a train station and international airport that travel to numerous destinations in France and Europe. Travel to Paris is possible in just 1h25 by high-speed train, from which even more travel options are possible.
I don't speak French, is that a problem?
With over 100 nationalities on campus, RSB is the perfect destination for English speakers. Outside the school, some basic phrases will enable you to live easily in the city, in which many people also speak English.

（格勒諾布爾-阿爾卑斯大學） 
地點 621 Av. Centrale, 38400 Saint-Martin-d'Hères, - France 
 
學校簡介 
（出處:維基
百科） 
格勒諾布爾-阿爾卑斯大學 （法語：Université Grenoble Alpes） 簡稱格勒諾布爾
大學、UGA， 是一所位於法國格勒諾布爾市的一流頂尖研究型大學。 最早成立
於 1339 年， 是法國第七大古老的大學， 也是法國規模第三大的高等教育學府，
擁有 4 萬多學生與 3 千多位研究員。格勒諾布爾市是歐洲最大的科學中心之
一，法國所有的國家研究機構皆位於此，整座城市有高達 22,800 位研究員，
因此格勒諾布爾大學也與數百所教研機構皆有建立合作關係，包括法國國家
科學研究中心（CNRS）和法國原子能和替代能源委員會（CEA）等代表性國家
研究機構。2019 年，格勒諾布爾大學獲選為法國四大國家級人工智慧研究中
心之一。 
 
格勒諾布爾大學的科學研究實力位於法國頂尖水準，誕生過三位諾貝爾獎得
主和一位圖靈獎得主，同時也是聯合國教科文組織國際傳播學教席所在地。

Exchange Students
Your admission - Step by step
Your home university has selected you for an exchange program at Lyon 3.
Lyon 3 International Office has received your nomination and all the necessary documents and information.
Lyon 3 International Office will verify your nomination and validate it if all requirements are met.
You will then receive an email containing the student number and password required for online registration.
If you are a non-European student, you will receive an acceptance letter that will enable you to apply for a visa.
Programs in French - DEUF
Programme d’Études Universitaires Françaises
Diplôme d’Études Universitaires Françaises
(DEUF) for one semester or a full year.
This program is offered to Bachelor and Masters students coming to study at Lyon 3 for a semester or a year and is run entirely in French. You can choose from classes belonging to different faculties and schools, including: business administration, philosophy, languages, law, political science, literature, information & communication, history, and geography. The B1 certificate is required for the Programme d'Études Universitaires Françaises students.
The following subjects are compulsory:
Français Langue Étrangère
(FLE): French as a Foreign Language
Initiation à la Culture Française
: Introduction to French Culture (
excl. law students
)
Méthodologie et Introduction au Droit
: Methodology and Introduction to Law (
for law and political science students only
)
►
Information Session
Information sessions are compulsory and take place at the beginning of the semester. At these sessions, you will receive a list of tutors who will assist you in choosing classes, registering online, and organizing your timetable. You will be informed of a session date upon arrival at the university.
► Erasmus+ Students
Erasmus+ students will also need to fill out a learning agreement.
>>> Check the program dates
Contact:
Romane Clauzel
deuf.scolarite@univ-lyon3.fr
Programs in English
SELF
SELF Program: Study in English in Lyon, France
This program, taught in English, is designed for undergraduate students who are not specialising in French. The program runs for one semester or a year and allows students to develop skills in law, business administration, and social sciences.
Language level required [except if the official language of your home University is English] TOEFL IBT:  overall score of 80 or higher with 20 at least for each section – only the official test will accepted (the local version is not adequate) TOEFL ITP: overall score of 560 minimum and 50 at least for each section IELTS Academic: overall score of 6,5 and no section score below 6 TOEIC including speaking, writing, listening and reading test: overall score of 1020 Cambridge Advanced: A/B Cambridge Proficiency: C minimum Duolingo English Test: overall score of 125
The tests listed above must have been undertaken no more than 2 years before starting the SELF program.
> More information
► Information Session
Information sessions are compulsory for newcomers and include a presentation on the SELF program and the university as a whole.
►
Orientation period
Orientation period
consists of a French placement test for the French language class, Introduction to Life in France and in Lyon, Intensive French language classes, a session on Digital Work Environment, a Campus Tour, and a Library Tour.
Contact:
Fanny SOUCHON
selfprogram@univ-lyon3.fr
iaelyon - School of Management
In the DEUF program
This program allows undergraduate and graduate
exchange students
who wish to follow English classes for one semester or a year in business administration and management.
Language level required
[except if the official language of your home University is English]
- TOEFL IBT: overall score of 80 or higher, with at least 20 for each section – only the official test will be accepted (the local version is not adequate)
- TOEFL ITP: overall score of 560 minimum and 50 at least for each section
- IELTS Academic: overall score of 6,5 and no section score below 6
- TOEIC, including speaking, writing, listening, and reading test: overall score of 1020
- Cambridge Advanced: A/B
- Cambridge Proficiency: C minimum
- Duolingo English Test: overall score of 125
The tests listed above must have been undertaken no more than 2 years before the commencement of the program.
Course selection is made on demand (depending on course availability). Check the
course catalogue
.

text:
【第1頁】
Application Guide
www.th-ab.de/eng  
✓ This handout will answer your first questions about applying to Aschaffenburg University of Applied 
Sciences as an exchange student. Check off each item once completed to help keep track of your progress.
Step 1: Nomination
We kindly ask all partner institutions to nominate their outgoing students by sending an email to incoming@
th-ab.de, stating the students‘ full name, gender, email address, field of studies and period of stay.
Step 2: Online Application
› Please go to www .th-ab.de/apply-online to access our online application. You will need to create a personal
account to access the application form.
› The following documents are to be uploaded during the online application:
Passport-style photo (i.e. digital portrait photo, coloured, JPG only) 
Scan of your passport / identity card
Current transcript of records from your home university
Erasmus+ or GJU students: learning agreement, signed by you and your home university 
EU-citizens: scan of your EU health insurance card (both sides).
› Once you submit the application online, a PDF document will be cr
eated. This may take a few minutes.
› Please print 
and sign the document on the last page under the “Declaration and Consent” section,
stating the date and place of the signature.
› Please email the signed application form to 
incoming@th-ab.de.
Step 3: Letter of Acceptance
The letter of acceptance is an electronic document issued by Aschaffenburg UAS, that contains your 
personal details as well as information about your exchange studies with us. If your application is 
successful, your letter of acceptance will be emailed to you after the application period.
Step 4: Semester Fee (“Studierendenwerksbeitrag”)
According to the Bavarian Higher Education Act, all students are to pay a small service fee for the adminis-
tration of certain services, such as the cafeteria or the halls of residence. Paying the semester fee is man-
datory for enrolment at Aschaffenburg UAS. Please note that the fee has to be paid before your arrival. Cur-
rently, the semester fee amounts to 70 EUR. Further information will be sent with the letter of acceptance.
Further Steps
Once you have been accepted and received your letter of acceptance, depending on where you are from, 
there are a few other formalities to take care of. We will send further information on applying for 
a visa, health insurance, and housing with your letter of acceptance. The halls of residence are run by 
Studierendenwerk Wuerzburg. We cannot guarantee a room in the halls and recommend looking for private 
accommodation as well. Please apply for the halls of residence by June 15 (for the winter semester) and

[重要提示]
請您注意，自2025年起學生簽證（德國高等學院正式學生與欲申請德國高等學院者）的申請將全部透過
Auslandsportal線上簽證系統
提出申請。本會僅提供非常少許零星的時段給申請者直到前來本會進行學生簽證申請。
在Auslandsportal線上簽證系統的文件審查確認無誤過後，申請者將會收到由該系統提供給您的簽證時段，前來現場提交生物特徵資料(按壓指紋以及護照照片)，以及繳交費用。因此，您無須另外在預約系統裡預約申請時段。
更多關於透過Auslandsportal線上簽證系統申請簽證之相關資訊，請您點選
這裡
。
一般須知
德國鼓勵有天賦且動機強烈之國際學生於德國高等學院就讀。入境德國前，您須取得必要之簽證**。唯有相責德國外事單位許可您的簽證申請，我們方能核發簽證。
(**澳洲，加拿大，以色列，日本，紐西蘭，南韓以及美國公民，可透過免簽的方式前往德國，並且可於入境德國之後(90天之內)直接於德國境內外事單位申請長期居留證。我們建議這些國家之公民，盡量於入境德國之後直接申請居留證。)
於您填寫簽證申請表格及預約時間之前，請您先準備好下列必備文件 (Checkliste):
有效護照
正本(須於最近十年內核發，持照人已於簽名處簽名, 至少須有兩頁以上空白頁面)
完整填寫好的
申請表格 (
表格
)
，一份
護照個人基本資料頁影本
，一份
兩張最新且符合生物特徵之
證件照
(須於三個月內拍攝)
非台灣籍：須檢附在台居留證(ARC)正本及影本一份
德國高等學院入學許可
, 一份
交換學生
須額外 檢附：
目前就讀之台灣學校所核發的
英文版在學證明
，一份
目前就讀之台灣學校所核發的
英文版成績單
，一份
***此項不適用於交換學生***
依據入學許可
授課語言能力證明
, 一份
(德語能力證明：例如 DSH, Goethe-Zertifikat, TestDaF；英語能力證明：例如 , IELTS, TOEFL,TOEIC)
財力證明
(需檢附第一年之財力證明。交換學生部份，請檢附總停留時間之財力證明)
每月
至少
992
歐元，一份
以簽證申請者為名開立之
限制提領帳戶(Sperrkonto)
，存款金額至少
11904
歐元(=12x992歐元)，或
政府立案機構之獎學金證明
(例如
DAAD
)
***此項不適用於交換學生***
至目前為止之中學學歷證明/高等學院學歷證明/技職教育結業證明，及在特定狀況下，其他與德國學業相關之資格證明，
正本及影本一份
德文
或
英文
動機信,一份
請詳細闡述至德國求學原因及該學業對於日後職業未來之影響
適用於德國境內，且於入境日開始生效之英文或德文版保險證明
，一份
Info
請您不要將簽證申請文件釘在一起!
若您提供非英文或德文之文件，則須同時附上相對應之譯本。
流程說明
請您遞交
完整申請文件
，因為僅在申請文件完備時，本會始得處理該申請。每個簽證申請將會個別被審核。依個案不同，可能會要求您提供其他文件及/或資訊。針對缺件之簽證申請，本會保有拒絕之權力。遞交所有被要求之文件，無法保證簽證一定會被核發。
財力證明：於簽證申請流程中，足夠財力可藉由開立
限制提領帳戶
(Sperrkonto)
來證明。您可自由選擇於德國境內之提供機構。提供該服務之機構請參考。
申請限制提領帳戶時，您需要護照正本，
請在提出簽證申請前
，
即完成開戶步驟
。最好的狀況是，於簽證面談當下即提交您的限制提領帳戶證明。
簽證處理費用
為75歐元，您可於面試當下以台幣現金支付。簽證申請一旦被受理，則費用將無法被退還 – 不論日後審核結果為何!
處理完整簽證申請之工作天，基本上大約為2到3週
；可能依個案不同而更久。德國在台協會無法干涉或是加快外事單位簽證審核程序。因此，德國在台協會請您於簽證申請過程中，不要詢問任何簽證進度相關問題。
當您的簽證申請流程結束時，本會將立即以信件方式通知您
。
關於德國境內就學必須擁有的健康保險，因於德國高等學院辦理註冊，須出示德國境內健保公司之保險證明，因此您必須購買德國境內公立保險公司或私人保險公司的產品。德國或其他國家提供的旅遊健康平安保險 無法用來辦理入學註冊手續。因此，請您儘早了解關於德國境內健保公司的相關產品(尤其是提供給學生的特殊優惠產品)。請您注意，您的健保必須於入境德國那一天生效。最理想的狀況是，您購買所謂的Incoming保險，此類保險於您入境德國的那一天生效，在您生病或受傷時，提供足夠的保障。並且在您正式註冊為學生後，直接自動轉換成德國境內的公立或私人學生健保，在這轉換的過程中，您的保險不會有任何的間斷。
依據外事單位許可，我們可核發
九十天或六個月不等
之
學生簽證
；入境德國後，您須持該簽證向當地外事單位提出長期居留證申請。對於交換學生，大部份我們可核發停留德國總時間(一或兩個學期)簽證。所有移居德國的人必須於兩週內於居住地所在之戶政單位辦理入戶登記。
可持學生簽證於求學期間工作？
可以，於高等學院辦理註冊後，您可持學生簽證/居留證工作，或從事學生工讀，一年總計最多可達120個全天或240個半天。該工作許可並不適用於學前準備課程(例如語言班)之停留。德國外事單位可額外增定限制條件，例如只能於學校放假期間(寒暑假期間)工作。
免除法律責任：本須知所列之內容，為撰寫此須知時所掌握之資訊。其完整性及正確性，尤其新釋出之相關規定，本會不賦與任何保證。

Fact Sheet on Student Exchange Program 
Academic year 2026/2027 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Contact information 
Name of university Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences (HKA) 
(Hochschule Karlsruhe (HKA))

 HKA International Program (English taught courses)

Email: internationalprogram@h-ka.de 
 (Contact person for Erasmus-OLA) 
Tel.: +49 (0)721 – 925 2506 
Erasmus code D KARLSRU05 
Website https://www.h-ka.de/en/io 
General information 
Academic calendar Winter Semester 2026/27 
September 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 
Summer Semester 2027 
March 1, 2027 – August 31, 2027 
Welcome and orientation phase September 11 – 27, 2026 Feb 26 – March 14, 2027 
Preparatory intensive German 
language course September 14 – 25, 2026 March 1 – March 12, 2027 
Teaching period  September 28, 2026 – January 22, 2027 
March 15 – July 2, 2027 
 
 


【第2頁】
Fact Sheet 2026/27 www.h-ka.de  
 
Examinations January 25 – February 12, 2027 July 05 – July 23, 2027 
Holidays / 
Semester Breaks 
December 22, 2026 – January 6, 2027 
(Christmas) 
April 03 – April 07, 2026 (Easter) 
June 09 – June 15, 2026 (Whitsun) 
Link to academic calendar https://www.h-ka.de/en/about-hka/news-events/academic-calendar/semester- 
dates#c39192 
Student workload The normal workload for full-time students is 30 ECTS credits per semester. 
Application + nomination deadline May 15 November 15 
Application procedure  Via online portal. Information at: https://www.h-ka.de/en/exchange-students 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Application process 
Requested application documents: 
• Learning agreement listing the course units that they wish to take1 
• Transcripts of Records obtained in previous years of study 
• Copy of passport 
If a student intends to do a thesis project at HKA or an internship in industry, a short 
description of the intended subject area of the thesis / the internship is required. 
Applications sent by post cannot be considered. 
Incomplete applications cannot be considered. 
It is very important that the applicants spell their full name as it appears on their 
passport, and that they attach a copy of their passport. 
Any delay in sending the documents may cause problems in finding accommodation. 
Students who need a visa should bear in mind that the visa application process may 
take up to ten weeks. We therefore strongly recommend that those students submit 
their application as early as possible, and no later than May 15 / November 15. 
Once we have received the complete application, we will forward it to the relevant 
Faculty for their assessment. This may take up to 6 weeks. As soon as the faculty has 
agreed to accept a student, we will issue the invitation letter. An electronic copy, which 
can be used for a visa application, will be sent to the student by e-mail. 
 
Language requirement 
For courses taught in German, a minimum language competency at CEFR (Common 
European Framework of Reference for Languages) B2 level is required. Likewise, for the 
International Program a minimum English language competency at CEFR B2 level is 
required. 
Students who do not fulfill the language requirement cannot be accepted. 
 
Can students extend their 
exchange period? 
Yes, but this would be subject to the approval of the home and host universities. 
Students may extend their stay for another study semester or for an internship in 
industry, provided they have been successful in finding a placement for themselves. 
HKA will assist exchange students in finding a place, but cannot provide internships 
itself. 
 
Activities or services available to 
exchange students 
• Access to campus facilities including library, student canteen, etc. 
• Buddy-program: buddies will help in administrative matters in the first weeks 
• Events and excursions for international students are offered at modest prices 
• Free limited semester ticket for the Karlsruhe Public Transport System KVV with the 
option to purchase a full semester ticket with a substantial student discount 
 
 
1 Note that here are courses for which, according to examination rules, only pass/fail grades are given. 
For information about German courses consult the module descriptions for the individual degree programs at https://www.h-ka.de/en/study. 
For HKA International Program courses there will be a remark in the Learning Agreement. 

【第3頁】
Fact Sheet 2026/27 www.h-ka.de  
 
Course-related information for exchange students 
Online course information https://www.h-ka.de/en/exchange-students 
Course schedule/timetable Will be provided upon arrival. 
Medium of instruction and 
assessment 
The medium of instruction and assessment for courses offered within the HKA 
International Program is English. For other courses it is German, unless specified 
otherwise. 
Minimum and maximum number of 
credits to be taken per semester 
Maximum number of ECTS credit points per semester: 30. Depending on approval by 
the sending institution, exchange students can take fewer credits, but not more. 
Are students allowed to take cross- 
faculty modules? 
Yes, subject to approval by the faculties involved. It is the student’s responsibility to 
make sure that this does not result in timetable clashes. 
 
Level of courses 
Exchange students normally take courses according to their academic level at their 
home institution. Advanced bachelor students may be eligible to take master’s courses, 
provided they meet the respective academic requirements. 
 
 
Language classes 
German Language Intensive Course starting approx. two weeks before lectures start 
(levels A 1 – B2.2). German language classes are also offered during the semester (level 
A 1 – B 2.2). All German language classes are free of charge for exchange students. For 
higher levels, students will be assisted in finding courses at other institutions. 
Other language courses including English, French and Spanish are offered to interested 
students free of charge at the HKA’s Foreign Language Institute (IFS). 
 
Transcripts 
HKA’s International Office will receive the official transcripts approx. 6- 7 weeks after 
end of examination period and will send them on to the sending institutions 
International Office by e-mail and, if requested, also in paper form. 
Accommodation 
 
 
Is university accommodation 
available for exchange students? 
There are 2 options: 
1. Students can apply for university accommodation directly at the Student Services 
Information: https://www.sw-ka.de/en/wohnen/ 
2. The International Office has a limited quota of rooms in student hostels. Students 
will receive information on how to apply for such a room with their invitation letter. 
These rooms can only be rented for one semester. 
Is university accommodation 
guaranteed? No, unfortunately we cannot guarantee it. 
Is accommodation available over 
semester breaks? University accommodation (option 2) can only be rented for a complete semester. 
Website for information on 
accommodation  For more information about accommodation: https://www.h-ka.de/en/accommodation 
Visa requirements 
Are exchange students required to 
obtain a student visa? 
Depends on nationality; information at www.auswaertiges- 
amt.de/EN/EinreiseUndAufenthalt/03_Visabestimmungen/Visabestimmungen_node.h 
tml 
Are exchange students allowed to 
work? 
Exchange students are expected to have a full study workload. In order for students to 
get the most out of their exchange academically, we cannot recommend working. 
However, they are usually allowed to work a maximum of 20h per week. 

【第4頁】
Fact Sheet 2026/27 www.h-ka.de  
 
Arrival / Orientation program 
Recommended arrival dates Winter Semester 
An orientation will take place the week 
before German intensive courses start 
To guarantee smooth enrolment we 
highly recommend that students arrive 
two weeks before lectures start. 
Summer Semester 
An orientation will take place the week 
before German intensive courses start 
To guarantee smooth enrolment we highly 
recommend that students arrive two weeks 
before lectures start. 
Is an airport pick-up service 
available? 
No, there isn’t. The train connections between Frankfurt airport and Karlsruhe are 
excellent, with trains running hourly during the daytime. 
Insurance 
Are exchange students required to 
purchase insurance? 
Yes. It is mandatory for enrollment. Since Winter Semester 2020/2021, there are new 
health insurance requirements for students under 30! 
1. Private health insurances will need to be approved by German statuary health insurance 
2. Students need a full coverage health insurance, including a nursing care 
insurance 
3. Valid health insurance is a prerequisite for enrolment and has to be taken care of 
before arrival. The cost is approx. € 120 per month. 
Estimated expenses in local currency 
(The estimated costs are for reference only. Actual expenses may vary from person to person.) 
• € 115 contribution fee for student services (Studierendenwerk) per semester 
• € 10 one-off fee for the campus card 
• Approx. € 390 for accommodation per month 
• Approx. € 140 for insurance per month 
• Approx. € 190 for public transport (depending on the student’s place of residence) per semester 
• Approx. € 90 for meals in the student canteen per month 
It is not possible to transfer payments in advance. Students must make sure they have sufficient financial means for meeting 
the costs above and living expenses once they are in Karlsruhe (details will be given by the International Office). 
 
Scholarship program for exchange students: https://www.bw-stipendium.de/en/ 
Contact person at HKA: Hannes Schwarz: hannes.schwarz@h-ka.de (students have to be nominated) 
German grading system 
Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences uses the following grading scheme: 
• 1,0 – 1,5 (Very good) 
• 1,6 – 2,5 (Good) 
• 2,6 – 3,5 (Satisfactory) 
• 3,6 – 4,0 (Sufficient) 
• 4,1 – 5,0 (non-sufficient / fail) 
Some courses at HKA are not graded and simply evaluated with “pass” or “fail”.

International applicants
Exchange students
You have studied at one of our numerous
partner universities
worldwide for at least two semesters and would now like to study for a semester at HKA under an exchange agreement? Or perhaps you would like to come for two semesters in order to do an internship in a German company after a semester of courses on our campus? Alternatively you would like to write your Bachelor's or Master's thesis at HKA in cooperation with your home university?
Here you can find out how to apply as an exchange student at HKA and get relevant information for your upcoming exchange.
Before your arrival
Which courses can I take?
When and how do I apply?
Which documents do I need?
What about accommodation?
After your arrival
Registering in Karlsruhe
Getting your residence permit
General information about Karlsruhe
Before leaving Karlsruhe
De-registering from HKA
De-registering from Karlsruhe
Transcript of Records
I want to stay longer!
Downloads and links
Before your arrival
Which courses can I take?
As an exchange student you have the opportunity to attend courses in German or in English and to receive credit at home for your achievements from one or two exchange semesters at HKA. Courses from our regular degree programs, which are usually taught in German, can be found
here
.
You will find a large selection of courses taught in English at our International Program:
Winter Semester
and
Summer Semester
.
For both languages, a language level of B2 (European Framework of Reference) is required.
By taking a German language course (two-week intensive course before the start of the semester and/or semester course) you can acquire 5 ECTS points.
When and how do I apply?
After your home university has nominated you for the exchange semester at HKA and you have agreed on a so-called Learning Agreement, you apply at HKA via the
application portal
of the International Office. The application deadline is November 15 for the summer semester and May 15 for the winter semester. If you need a visa, you should allow approximately 10 weeks for this and apply in due time.
Please ask your home university coordinator for advice on the exact application procedure and your learning agreement. Important: Some courses at HKA are not graded with a mark, but with pass/fail.
Which documents do I need?
For your application:
Filled-in learning agreement; Erasmus Students can send their Online Learning Agreement (OLA) via the EWP-dashboard instead. In that case, please just upload a document stating “OLA via EWP dashboard” in the online portal. (The normal semester workload is 30 credit points (CP) according to ECTS, in accordance with your home university, you can take less CP but not more).
current transcript of records / transcript of grades from your university
for thesis or internship semester: short description of the planned topic
copy of your passport
Other important documents:
Visa: an overview of visa regulations can be found
here
. Soon after your application you will receive an invitation letter which you should use to start the visa process as soon as possible. We collected some helpful
here
and
this page
has proofen to be very helpful.
Since recently,
proof of insurance
is a mandatory part of enrolment at German universities. Therefore this needs to be taken care of before your arrival as well (by July for winter semester or January for summer semester).
Students with disabilities or chronic illnesses can find information on disadvantage compensation (e.g. for exams) or accessibility
here
. Please contact the International Office as early as possible - ideally already during the application process - to apply for compensation for disadvantages.
What about accommodation?
We strongly recommend starting your room search as early as possible.
On this site
you'll find a lot of helpful links.
After your arrival
Registering in Karlsruhe
Everybody has to register with the city of Karlsruhe (Bürgerbüro/Einwohnermeldeamt) within two weeks after moving into his or her apartment/room. Please note that you also have to notify the Bürgerbüro/Einwohnermeldeamt every time you change your address in Germany. To get registered you need to make an appointment
here
(you might have to reload the page). Choose “Meldewesen”- Zuzug nach Karlsruhe" (the first option under "Meldewesen"), click "Weiter", in the calendar you'll see the next available appointments. You can do the registration at any office (K8 is closest to the University). Confirm your choice ("Termin wählen") and  fill in your information and click on "Weiter".
You will receive a confirmation mail with a booking number. Keep that number safe and  and be sure to cancel the appointment if you are unable to go! You should be at the appoinment 15 Minutes early.
You will need the following documents:
Your passport
Wohnungsgeberbestätigung / Landlord certificate (This form has to be filled out and signed by your landlord, you can find it under
Formulare
. Unfortunately, all forms are only available in German).
This is not your rental contract!
If applicable: your residence permit or visa
At the end you will receive a Registration Confirmation - make sure to keep this document safe!
Getting your residence permit
All non-EU exchange students
either need to have a visa that covers the whole exchange period or a valid residence permit for studying purposes. This means that if your visa expires before the end of your exchange stay, you will need to apply for a residence permit for studying purposes before the expiry date of your visa.
You will need to submit the following documents (copies) to the Ausländerbehörde (foreigners office):
copy of your current visa for Germany (if applicable)
copy of your passport
proof of sufficient funds to cover all expenses during your stay in Germany (at least 992 € monthly, e.g. blocked bank account or official statement of your scholarship)
"Immatrikulationsbescheinigung" (Proof of enrollment)
proof of health insurance (confirmation issued by your insurance provider)
You should also compile and upload:
confirmation of your registration as a resident of the city of Karlsruhe (see
above
)
copy of your rental contract
any further confirmation that can support your application (e.g. confirmation about the extension of your exchange semester)
You can fill in the application online
here
(choose option 1 - residence permit for training) and upload all your documents there. Make sure to note down your Application-Number at the end and that you really receive a confirmation mail.
The processing of applications currently takes about 10 weeks
, so it is important to submit your application as early as possible. You will receive their decision via post or e-mail. After receiving their decision, you can make an
appointment
to submit the biometric data (fingerprints and photo - choose "Abgabe biometrischer Daten"). At this appointment they will order your new electronic residence permit. The cost of the permit is around 100€.
Should you not be able to submit everything via the link above, you can send your documents via mail (as one pdf) by email to
abh
spam prevention
@oa.karlsruhe.de
. You will need to add the filled in application form (click
here
and choose "Antrag auf Erteilung einer Aufenthaltserlaubnis" under "Formulare"). Make sure that your application is complete and save the automatically sent confirmation of receipt afterwards. Please be aware that sending the application via e-mail can lead to longer processing times.
General information about Karlsruhe
Check this
website
to learn about public transport system, recreational activities, doctor offices and more!
Before leaving Karlsruhe
De-registering from HKA
Once your stay at HKA is unfortunately coming to an end, we kindly ask you to request your de-registration (Exmatrikulation) from HKA to avoid any issues after your return. You will also need your "Exmatrikulationsbescheinigung" if you want to study at any German university again.
In order to ex-matriculate please get the signature from the library and send the signed
request for exmatriculation
via e-mail to
incoming
spam prevention
@h-ka.de
or upload it on the Hisinone portal. A few days later, you can download the de-registration certificate on Hisinone. You can also send the form before your departure, as the deregistration will only take effect after August 31st and has no influence on the current semester.
De-registering from the city
You have to notify the city of Karlsruhe that you are leaving the city. This can be done from one week before leaving until two weeks afterwards and is in your best interest because you also want to de-register from paying the Rundfunkbeitrag and avoid issues, should you ever travel to Germany again.
The de-regsitration can be done online, via post or in Person. To de-register from the city open
Onlineanträge "Ins Ausland abmelden"
and either make an appointment or download the form to send it via post.
To de-register from paying the Rundfunkbeitrag you can simply follow the steps
on their website
(again - this is all in German).
You should also inform your German health insurance provider a few days before you leave, so that you do not have to pay more than you need.
Transcript of Records
You can download your transcript of records
here
. Choose “Meine Funktionen” - click “Prüfungsverwaltung” on the left side - click “Bescheinigungen“ - choose the document/report you need (“Notenspiegel” = contains all courses you took, also the ones you failed. Only available in German | ECTS-Leistungsnachweis (Transcript of records) = does not include failed courses; comes with English translation). Some courses need to be added manually for exchange students. Therefore, the transcript is sometimes not complete even after the deadline to enter grades. Should you encounter any issues with your transcript, please contact us. Around mid-August or the beginning of March your transcript will also be send to your coordinator at your home university.
I want to stay longer
We are happy to know that you are enjoying your time at HKA and decided to extend your stay for a second semester.
Please inform us in the International Office at the latest by the end of June or the beginning of January, should you wish to extend your stay. You also need your home university's approval and please ask them to send a confirmation email to HKA's International Office.
Please send us the following documents via mail:
Enrollment certificate from your home university for the period you want to extend your stay (Please notice that you need to be enrolled at your home university for the entire duration of your stay at HKA)
A new learning agreement signed and stamped from your home university or a confirmation about your internship
Important: For your second semester at HKA, you must pay the student services fee of 108.70 EUR within the re-registration period.Don't forget to inform your health insurance provider in time and, if necessary, also the immigration office to extend your residence permit.

application deadlines 
 
 
 
 
2027:

exceptional cases and requires prior consultation. In such

International Office DHBW Loerrach V1.

3

should be submitted well in time (8-12 weeks before 
semester start or earlier) after receipt of Letter of 
acceptance from DHBW Loerrach. A Schengen Visa is 
recommended.

meet the Visa requirements before you apply. 
 
Registration at the Federal 
Office of Migration and 
Refugees (BAMF)

program or the agreement between the universities

(= 6 months)

mandatory service charges that all enrolled students at DHBW 
Loerrach are required to pay.

mandatory:

negligence or otherwise.

a further private insurance is recommended.

against loss through accidental bodily injury to the insured. 
Contact us. 
 
Travel cancellation insurance 
recommended: 
A travel cancellation insurance covers all possible travel 
arrangements in case of changes in plan.

activities, socializing and

 must have confirmed accommodation before arrival.

Laptop is essential.  
 
Psychotherapeutic Counseling: Psychotherapeutic counseling is available for students at all 
 DHBW university locations, offering confidential individual 
 support and workshops on successful studying.

confidential setting. These coaching and counseling sessions 
are free of charge and confidential.

Dear students, 
I welcome you at the DHBW Loerrach!
More than 34,000 students are enrolled at 
the 9  locations of the DHBW in Germany. 
The number of  companies and institu-
tions collaborating with the DHBW state 
university system exceeds 10,000.
DHBW Loerrach is a very special  location, 
only a bike-ride away from Switzerland 
and France. Our 2,100 students appre-
ciate the chance to study at  a  modern 
campus  in  an international  environment  
in  the heart of Europe. 
Internationalization is more than a 
keyword of our strategy, demonstrated by 
tri- and binational study programs, 
Business Management courses in English 
language and collaborations with more 
than 40 universities worldwide. Our 
students come from nearly 45 countries 
and this, too, contributes to the interna-
tional environment of the DHBW.
We believe in the importance of an 
international experience and intercultural 
competence of every student. This 
prepares the students to act and work in a 
globalized world.
Welcome Address by the President
One of our top priorities is on the one 
hand to develop student mobility and on 
the other to make our international 
students feel at home at the campus and 
in the city of Loerrach.
We wish you a wonderful and exciting 
time at DHBW Loerrach.
Prof. Gerhard Jäger, 
President DHBW Loerrach

 " 85 % of the DHBW students, who 
complete their studies and achieve 
a Bachelor's Degree, get the offer 
of a contract of employment by 
their partner companies.
Baden-Wuerttemberg Cooperative State 
University (Duale Hochschule Baden-
Württemberg / DHBW ) is the first higher 
education institution in Germany which 
combines on-the-job training and 
academic studies and, therefore, achieves 
a close integration of theory and practice, 
both components of cooperative 
education. 
The dual training system is based on the 
regular shift between academic studies at 
the university and practical training at the 
individual company. That means, students 
are not only taught theoretical knowledge, 
but also learn to apply this knowledge in 
practice. 
As one of the nine locations of the DHBW, 
Loerrach offers a broad range of 
undergraduate study programs in the 
fields of business and engineering. All 
degree programs are both nationally and 
internationally accredited, count as 
intensive study programs and students 
acquire 210 ECTS credits.
About the DHBW Loerrach

All courses at the DHBW Loerrach start on 
October 1st each year. As our programs 
incorporate theory and practice, our 
academic year is divided into 3–4 
quarters, where students alternate 
between studying on campus and working 
in a partner company. International 
students have the chance to acquire up to 
30 ECTS during one quarter. Students 
from any of our partner universities are 
exempted from the payment of tuition 
fees at DHBW.

DHBW Loerrach has three campuses: 
one at Hangstrasse, another one, the 
so called „KBC“, at Marie-Curie-

on a hillside over-looking the city of

LIVING COSTS
The living costs in Loerrach are estimated 
between 1.000 – 1.500 Euros per month. 
These costs include housing, food, social 
activities, travel and so on. Please make 
sure to have sufficient money available to 
spend the time here without financial 
straits.
REGISTRATION AT  
CITY HALL LOERRACH
Once you have arrived in Loerrach, you 
have to register at the City Hall. The 
following documents are necessary for 
the registration: your passport, your visa 
(if you have one), the completed 
registration form, the rental contract. You 
have to inform the City Hall every time 
you move to a another place in Loerrach. 
That means that you also have to 
de-register again when you return to your 
home country, after your semester at our 
university is over.
BAMF REGISTRATION
Registration at Federal Office for Migration 
and Refugees (BAMF) for students from 
countries outside the European Union, 
who wish to stay up to 360 days in 
Germany for study purposes:
If you already hold a residence title issued 
by another Member State for study 
purposes, you do not require a German 
residence title, but your residence title 
must be valid for the entire duration of 
your stay in Germany.
The German higher education institution 
must submit prior notification of your 
intended stay to the Federal Office for 
Migration and Refugees. This notification 
should be provided as soon as it becomes 
known that you intend to study in 
Germany. Full notification absolutely must 
be received no later than 30 days prior to 
your entering Germany.
The Federal Office for Migration and 
Refugees will issue you with a certificate 
confirming your entitlement to stay in 
Germany.

BADEN-WUERTTEMBERG
Loerrach is situated in the federal state of 
Baden-Wuerttemberg, which ranks among 
Europe‘s leaders in technology and 
maintains long traditions of innovation 
and creativity.
Impressive brands such as Porsche and 
Mercedes-Benz have headquarters and 
museums located in the region. The 
capital, Stuttgart, is home to one of the 
largest zoos and botanical gardens in 
Europe. Stuttgart is a popular destination 
for our students due to its nearby location 
and entertainment possibilities. 
The people in Baden-Wuerttemberg 
benefit of an outstanding quality of life. 
People feel at home, enjoying a rich 
beautiful landscape and a lively internati-
onal arts and culture scene. They profit 
from the community’s outstanding 
environmental values.
With its 11 million inhabitants, Baden- 
Württemberg is the third largest of the 16 
German federal states. Nearly 1.2 million 
residents are of non-German origin, 
mostly Turkish, Greek and Italian. 
Baden-Württemberg also enjoys one the 
lowest unemployment rates of any 
German federal state. This makes it a 
perfect location for students, who want to 
build their careers. 
LOERRACH
Loerrach is a small city in the south of 
Germany near the borders to Switzerland 
and France. This contributes to the 
outstanding character of the region. 
Loerrach has many attractions like the 
ruins of Roetteln Castle from the 11th 
Century. This castle is situated on a hilltop 
overlooking Loerrach and the valley of the 
river Wiese. Parkschwimmbad, a huge 
outdoor swim area, is another large 
attraction of Loerrach’s, with a wave 
machine, water slides, diving platforms 
and an exercise pool. It’s great to be there 
on a bright day together with friends. 
Besides Loerrach has an impressive 
concert hall, the Burghof, the picturesque 
river Wiese and many large companies.

Application and Admission for Programme Students
Application and Admission for Programme Students
Programme Students
Erasmus study abroad experiences, student exchanges under a partnership/student exchange agreement (incl. the Coimbra Group Student Exchange Network and the Swiss European Mobility Programme), holders of scholarships or grants provided by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), Fulbright, FGAC; please enquire about other programmes.
If your home university does not have a partnership agreement with the University of Würzburg and you have not been selected for a scholarship programme, under certain conditions it is possible to spend an exchange semester at the University of Würzburg as a so-called
freemover
.
1. Application an nomination via your home university
You will have to apply directly to your home university/the scholarship or grant sponsor.
If you are selected for participation, your home university/sponsor* will nominate you to us.
Deadlines for nominations to the University of Würzburg:
30 April for winter intake
30 November for summer intake
Find out what
language requirements
you will have to meet to qualify for admission as an exchange student.
AFTER your home university/sponsor has nominated you to us, we will email you a link that will take you to our online registration form.
*Some sponsors do not contact the host universities with nominations. If that is the case for your sponsor, please email us at
exchange-international@uni-wuerzburg.de
before the deadline for nominations has passed and let us have a letter from your sponsor confirming that they have awarded the scholarship or grant to you.
2. Fill registration form
AFTER your home university/sponsor has nominated you to us, we will email you a link that will take you to our online registration form.
Deadlines for online registration
15 June for winter intake
15 January for summer intake
Please contact us if you are unable to meet this deadline.
Please register as soon as possible after you receive our email.
Please note
The application deadlines for rooms in
student residences
are 15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester! You will NOT have to supply a letter of admission when you apply for a room in a student residence.
Please be aware that there is a special application process in place for exchange students. We will send you the relevant instructions after we have received your nomination.
You will have to attach the following documents when registering online:
An enrolment certificate issued by your home university
A transcript of records issued by your home university that documents your academic achievements to date
Proof of your proficiency in the German language (if you are not holding an official German language certificate, you can ask one of the German teachers at your home university to issue you with a letter to confirm that you have the required German language skills;
template letter
)
Proof of your proficiency in the English language (if you are not holding an official English language certificate, you can ask one of the English teachers at your home university to issue you with a letter to confirm that you have the required English language skills;
template letter
)
Only required if you are doing an exchange programme other than Erasmus
: If you are doing a student exchange at the University of Würzburg under a partnership agreement: a list of the courses you want to take at the University of Würzburg (course selection list;
template and more information
)
Information regarding language certificates
We do not accept OLS test certificates as proof of your language skills.
3. Admission to the University of Würzburg as an programme student
Once we have received your online registration, the team at the International Office Incoming will review the information and documents you have supplied and will then issue you with a letter of admission to the University of Würzburg as an exchange student. We usually start sending out our letters of admission in June (for winter intake) or, respectively, in December (for summer intake). They are sent by email. Along with your letter of admission, you will receive more information about your stay at the University of Würzburg.
4. Enrolment
You can enrol through the online platform of the University of Würzburg
WueStudy
. You will receive all the information needed on your Admission Letter. Feel free to contact our staff and our
tutors
if you need a helping hand. You will receive your student ID card and semester ticket a few days after enrolment.
Further information for enrolment
Fact sheet for exchange students
Important
Please note that these instructions apply for exchange students only, i.e. students staying for up to 2 semesters and not seeking a degree at the University of Würzburg.

Dieser Nachweis kann nur durch einen Sprachlehrer ausgefüllt werden, nicht durch den Studierenden 
selbst.

valid language certificate. In order to take German courses at the Centre for Languages, a

Liste der geplanten Kurse 
List of planned courses 
 
Die Kursliste ist nicht verbindlich, sondern ermöglicht der Universität Würzburg vorab einen 
Überblick über die von Ihnen eingeplanten Kurse. 
Erasmus-Studierende, die ein Learning Agreement für die Dauer ihres Aufenthalts an unserer 
Hochschule abschließen müssen, brauchen dieses Dokument nicht auszufüllen. 
Diese Liste ersetzt nicht die Registrierung für die Kurse in WueStudy. 
The courses listed below are not compulsory, they are only meant to give the University of Würzburg 
an overview of the courses planned by the student. 
Erasmus students who have to submit a Learning Agreement for the duration of their stay at our 
University do not have to fill in this document. 
This list does not replace the the registration for the courses in WueStudy. 
 
Nutzen Sie für die Kurswahl das Vorlesungsverzeichnis des vergangenen 
Winter/Sommersemesters in WueStudy und tragen Sie Ihre Präferenzen hier ein. Bitte 
beachten Sie, dass es zu Änderungen im Vorlesungsverzeichnis kommen kann und Sie Ihre 
Kurswahl ggf. nach Ihrer Ankunft ändern müssen. Die Änderungen müssen dem International 
Office Incoming nicht mitgeteilt werden. 
You can search for courses in WueStudy via the course catalogue of the previous winter/summer 
semester and list your preferred courses on this form. Please note that if changes are made to the 
course catalogue, you may have to change your course selection. The International Office Incoming 
does not need to be informed of the changes.

Learning Agreement
Course schedule information for international exchange students (e.g. ERASMUS)
Tips:
In the
module descriptions and handbooks
, you will find additional information, also available in English.
Please contact the academic coordinator; they can recommend suitable courses for you.
You can also use the previous year's schedule as a reference
1. Open the online course catalogue
Open the
course catalogue
.
Important:
Choose the right Semester! You can use our
video tutorials
(course management) to become familiar with our course catalogue.
Tip:
Always choose the programme with the higher number of ECTS. All courses included in programmes with fewer credits are also included in this programme.
2. Important hints
You’re also allowed to take courses for students of all subjects ("Veranstaltungen für Hörer/-innen aller Fakultäten")
(e.g. for language courses, etc.).
To find English taught courses, please use the Advanced Search function and select English as the teaching language.
You will be admitted to the major specified in your application (ERASMUS according to the bilateral agreement), but as an exchange student you can also attend courses in other subjects. However, in some courses it could be required to have previous knowledge of the subject. You can ask the lecturer.
Language courses start with a placement test. With the help of this placement test you will be assigned to a course that corresponds to your language level. This means that the course level you specify in your Learning Agreement might change after the test.
3. Tips to understand the terms used
By clicking on a course, you get further information. This table will help you to understand the terms used.
4. Complete the Learning Agreement and register for courses
Complete your Learning Agreement with the chosen courses. Changes to the chosen courses in the Learning Agreement are possible after arrival in Würzburg at any time and on previous arrangement with the Coordinator (“changes to the original Learning Agreement”).
At the University of Würzburg, the Learning Agreements will be signed by the
departmental coordinators
.
You know if you need a Learning Agreement for your home university. If your home university doesn’t need one, the University of Würzburg doesn’t need it either.
You can get advice from the
coordinators
,
the academic advisor center
or from the
faculties
concerning the study focus, course catalogue , etc.

Enrolment & Semester Fees
Enrolment & Semester Fees
Online enrolment/ online registration
1. Online-Enrolment
You can do the
online enrolment
for the winter term 2026/27  starting from July  22st via
online portal for enrolment
of the University of Würzburg.
2. Hand in documents
As part of the online enrolment you have to
upload on the portal Wuestudy the following documents:
Letter of Acceptance / Letter of Admission
Proof of payment of the semester fee (see below)
Copy of your passport
Kindly send
by email
to the International Students Office the
PDF of your Online Enrolment
so we can proceed your enrolment.
Contact a german statutory
health insurance
as a
digital confirmation
about your health insurance status is requiered as part of your enrolment.
As soon as we received and checked your documents we will complete your enrolment and inform you when your student card is ready to be picked up.
With the
student card
, you can:
Use all local
public transportation
in Würzburg. You can find further information about the semester ticket and a plan of the routes for which your ticket is valid
on
Studierendenwerk's website
.
Make cashless payments in the
cafeterias
and copy and print stations at the University of Würzburg;
Borrow library items from the
university libraries.
Semester Fee
There are no study fees at the University of Würzburg.
All students must, however, pay a semester fee of
€ 182,10
before they can be enrolled (Break down of the fee: Student Services fee: € 72.00 + semester ticket: € 110,10)
You can pay this amount before or after your arrival in Würzburg. It is important that you
transfer the amount before your enrollment
and
submit the proof of payment
at the International Office Incoming (see above).
The semester fee can only be paid by bank transfer. Bank transfer details will be included with your Letter of Acceptance.

Costs and Financing
Costs and Financing
Costs
Semester Contribution
There are no tuition fees at the University of Würzburg. However you must pay the semester contribution each semester for enrollment or re-enrollment. The semester contribution consists of a student contribution and the semester ticket.
More detailed information and the current amount of the semester contribution can be found on the websites of the Registrar’s Office.
Living Costs
The living costs in Würzburg are low compared to other German cities. Of course this also depends strongly on the individual life style, but you should expect monthly costs of about €940.
Eating
250,00 €
Living
350,00 €
Health Insurance
110,00 €
Other
212,00 €
Broadcasting fees (AZDBS/GEZ)*
18,00 €
Total
940,00 €
Further information can be found on the
website of DAAD
.
Broadcasting Fee (GEZ)
If you are staying in Germany longer than three months, you have to pay a broadcasting fee. The registration form can be found
online
.
Monthly fee: 18,36 €
Note
: In a shared flat (WG), the broadcasting fee contribution is a monthly fee for the whole apartment. Talk with your roommates about how you will apportion the fees.
Information and forms
Financing
Scholarships
You can finance your studies or doctoral studies in Germany with the help of scholarships. There are two possibilities to receive a scholarship:
In your home country
: Ask your home university about university partnership scholarships, Erasmus etc. You can also inform yourself about scholarships offered by the Ministry of Education or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
In Germany:
The
database of the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD)
provides an overview of scholarships for foreign students and doctoral candidates. The DAAD also has
offices abroad
where you can get information before departure.
On this website you can find
further information on scholarships
.
Another database for scholarships is
Stipendienlotse
ERASMUS-Mobility-Grant
If you need further information please ask your home University.
Working while you study
If you want to work while you are studying in Germany, please note the following information:
Students from countries within the EU and the EEA
are on equal terms on the labor market and are allowed to work during studies;
Students from other countries
are allowed to work 120 days of full-time work or 240 half days per year (which also concludes voluntary internships). If you would like to work more you need a permission from the agency for employment (Agentur für Arbeit) or the immigration office;
Important: Be sure your studies do not suffer if you have a side job! Please read the information
on the legal framework of the DAAD.
On the following pages you can search for job opportunities in Würzburg:
Federal Employment Agency
(Bundesagentur für Arbeit);
http://www.wuewowas.de/kle/nbj_list.php;
Unterfrankenjobs
;
Career Centre at the University of Wuerzburg;
https://www.jobbörse-stellenangebote.de/stellenangebote-würzburg/
In the pubs, restaurants and cafes in the city of Würzburg;
Student assistant positions at the University of Würzburg

WARNING: Please beware of tricksters on the housing market. Do NOT transfer high amounts of deposits beforehand!
Please note:
The University of Würzburg solely provides information for websites and third-party housing offers on the International Office website. The University of Würzburg is not responsible for the content of the respective websites and housing offers. The International Office does not act as an intermediary.
The University assumes no responsibility for the success of finding accommodation. JMU is also not liable for the content of the information provided by the potential tenants as third parties, nor for any possible damages resulting from the use of the information.
Advantage for exchange programme students:
Apply for a room in a dormitory of the Studierendenwerk by the official application deadline (15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester) and your accommodation is guaranteed!
Freemovers
can also apply for a room in a dormitory of The Studierendenwerk, but no room can be guaranteed.
Dormitories of the Student Housing Service (Studierendenwerk)
The
Student Housing Service
is responsible for several dormitories in various locations in Würzburg.
Amenities:
Single and double rooms or rooms in apartments where two to four students share a kitchen and bathroom;
All rooms and apartments are furnished;
Dishes, cooking items, bedding, and towels are not provided;
You can find more information about the individual dormitories on
Studierendenwerk's website
.
Length of stay:
Student accommodations are granted for 6 months (for one semester stay) or 12 months (for one year stay). A shorter rental period is not possible
Participants who participate in the intensive language course
before the semester begins can get a dorm room one month earlier, so that the length of the contract increases to 7 or 13 months
Application:
Deadlines:
June 15 for the Winter Semester and January 15 for the Summer Semester
(Student Housing Service must receive the security deposit by this date);
After your application as an exchange student, you'll will get from us a guide on "How to apply for a room in a dormitory?".
Please apply for a room in a dormitory as soon as you have the guide.
As an exchange student, you do NOT need your letter of acceptance for the dormitory application!
Programme students who apply online by this date are guaranteed to get a dorm room.
Please contact the
Student Housing Service
for any questions regarding your application for a dormitory.
Withdrawal from contract:
Reimbursement of the deposit is only possible within a certain time frame. Please see the Housing Office's website for
further information
.
To increase your chances of getting a room offer, we recommend choosing "single room in any shared apartment" as wished type of housing and for wished student residences "all with single rooms in any shared apartment in Würzburg"
