DORMITORY 
International House I-wing Nakamozu: https://www.omu.ac.jp/international/int_student/housing/i-wing-nakamozu/ 
【Rent】 
46,000 yen/month [Breakdown]  Rent 34,000 yen + common expenses (electricity and water included) 12,000 yen 
【Initial cost】 *Depends on length of stay 
67,000-68,000 yen [Breakdown] Security deposit 46,000 yen + Move-out Cleaning Fee 17,000 yen  
+  Insurance premium approx. 4,000-5,000 yen 

【第3頁】
 *As a rule, the deposit is applied to the payment of the final month's dormitory fees if there is no outstanding 
balance at the time of moving out. 
【Initial cost】 
・Information regarding dormitory application will be provided when the letter of acceptance is sent, so please do 
not apply for the dormitory on your own. 
 ・Applicants for I-wing Nakamozu must submit a health certificate. Early preparation is highly recommended. 
【NOTE】 
・As a rule, exchange students are expected to stay at the International House I-wing Nakamozu on the Nakamozu 
Campus. 
*Due to the limited number of rooms, we cannot guarantee occupancy. We may also guide you to other dormitories.  
*We do not provide support for off-campus housing. 
・If the Sugimoto Campus or Morinomiya Campus is your main campus, please use the campus shuttle bus or public 
transportation. 
*The travel time from I-wing Nakamozu to Morinomiya Campus is about 1 hour. 
*If you use only the subway OSAKA METRO, you will need to pay about 340 yen for one-way transportation. In case of 
a commuter pass, about 12,000 yen per month is needed. 
*Depending on the route used, a one-way ticket may cost about 500 yen, while a commuter pass may require 16,000 
to 18,000 yen. 
*Exchange students are not eligible to purchase a “student commuter pass”. When purchasing a commuter pass, it 
must be a “regular commuter pass. 
・A new international student residence, OMU I-Dorm Sugimoto ( https://dormy-ac.com/page/omu-
ac/properties/kokusai-kouryu/), is expected to open on the Sugimoto Campus in April 2027. Detailed information 
regarding student dormitory will be provided together with the acceptance notification. 
 
COURSE *Please note that this information is current as of now and is subject to change.  
・Details on course registration will be announced separately in mid-to-late March. 
・Undergraduate students take “Liberal Arts and Sciences Subjects.” In principle, they cannot take specialized 
courses. Master's students take “specialized courses.

Graduate students：https://www.omu.ac.jp/campus-life/course/academic-calendar/timetable-g/  
Syllabus Search：https://catalog.sp.omu.ac.jp/search 
 
TRANSCRIPT 
Academic transcripts (in English) will be sent in PDF to your university coordinator after completing the exchange 
program. 
*A semi-annual transcript will not be issued for one-year acceptance. 
*If you need the grades by semester, students can check them on the student portal.  
 
CERTIFICATE OF ELIGIBILITY（COE） 
・OMU will apply for the COE on behalf of students to the Immigration Services Agency. 
*Necessary documents for application will be announced separately sent to the coordinator. 
*Issuance of COE is subject to review by the Immigration Services Agency. OMU cannot guarantee the issuance or  

【第4頁】
timing of COE. The COE may be delayed if the Immigration Services Agency takes a long time to review the 
application of COE. 
・Japanese nationals (including dual nationals) are not eligible to apply for COE since they enter the country as 
Japanese nationals. Information on procedures after entry into Japan will be provided separately. 
 
ISSUANCE OF LETTER OF ACCEPTANCE 
OMU will issue a Letter of Acceptance (PDF) as soon as the acceptance is decided. 
Please note that we cannot answer inquiries regarding the selection process. 
*The acceptance may be canceled if any false information is found in the application. 
 
VISA APPLICATION 
Please print out the LOA and COE and apply for the visa at the Japanese Embassy or Consulate.  
*It may take some time to apply for a visa, so please apply well in advance. 
*Some foreign embassies may require an appointment for visa application, so please check by yourself. 
*Please purchase your airline ticket after obtaining a visa. 
 
ORIENTATION FOR EXCHANGE STUDENTS 
・After arriving in Japan, an orientation regarding life in Japan will be provided. 
・Orientation includes an explanation of city hall procedures and campus services. 
・In addition, we will hold various orientations such as “Orientation for I-wing Nakamozu Residents”.  
 
SCHEDULE FROM APPLICATION TO END OF STUDY PERIOD（Reference） 
All times are in Japan time.  *The timing may be slightly earlier or later due to procedural reasons. 
 Item Timeline  
 ➀ Start of recruitment. End of August 2026  
 ➁ Nomination Deadline. October 1, 2026  
 ➂ Deadline for submission of application documents October 10, 2026

 ➅ Certificate of eligibilities sent Mid-to-late February 2027  
 ➆ Entry Date (planned) March 30, 2027  
 ➇ Start of classes Early April 2027  
 ➈ Exam period *You can return home country after the exam. Late July - Early August 2027  
 ➉ Issuance of transcripts Early October 2027  
 
CONTACT  
国際戦略推進室 OMU Global Education TEL: +81-6-6167-1096  /  Email: gr-glo-inbound@omu.ac.jp

All inquiries must be made through your home university's coordinator.

Exchange program for the Spring 2027 Semester 
 
 
SUMMARY 
〈Website〉 https://www.omu.ac.jp/en/ 
Exchange Program：https://www.omu.ac.jp/international/int_student/exchangeprogram/  
〈Length of study〉 【1 Semester】 April 1, 2027～September 23, 2027

〈Acceptable 
qualifications〉 
Undergraduate students, 
Master’s students 
〈Nationality〉 No restrictions 
〈Notes〉 
*In principle 
・In this program, Undergraduate students will enroll at the “Faculty of Liberal Arts, Sciences 
and Global Education” and master's students will enroll at the “Graduate Schools”, Students 
will take regular courses together with OMU students.  
・Since all classes are conducted in Japanese (with the exception of some graduate courses), a 
Japanese language proficiency level equivalent to CEFR B2 or higher is required.
（Correspondence of the JLPT Total Score to the CEFR Level ） 
・OMU will decide the school/college/graduate school to which students belong based on their 
application documents. 
・We do not accept application for exchange program in the fields of Medicine, Nursing,  
Veterinary Science, Rehabilitation Science. 
・We don't have Department of Japanese Studies. 
・Graduate School of Informatics basically offers classes online. 
・We do not provide guidance on graduation thesis or graduation research. 
・It is not possible to change the acceptance period. 
・Students must return home country by the end of the semester. *Students cannot continue 
to stay in Japan.

students

campuses depending on the field of study. 
  We will inform you of each campus when we decide to accept students.

〈Nomination〉 by October 1, 2026  〈Application〉  by October 10, 2026

Early August(Spring semester completion)

【Rent】 
46,000 yen/month [Breakdown]  Rent 34,000 yen + common expenses (electricity and water included) 12,000 yen 
【Initial cost】 *Depends on length of stay 
67,000-68,000 yen [Breakdown] Security deposit 46,000 yen + Move-out Cleaning Fee 17,000 yen  
+  Insurance premium approx. 4,000-5,000 yen

 *As a rule, the deposit is applied to the payment of the final month's dormitory fees if there is no outstanding 
balance at the time of moving out. 
【Initial cost】 
・Information regarding dormitory application will be provided when the letter of acceptance is sent, so please do 
not apply for the dormitory on your own. 
 ・Applicants for I-wing Nakamozu must submit a health certificate. Early preparation is highly recommended. 
【NOTE】 
・As a rule, exchange students are expected to stay at the International House I-wing Nakamozu on the Nakamozu 
Campus. 
*Due to the limited number of rooms, we cannot guarantee occupancy. We may also guide you to other dormitories.  
*We do not provide support for off-campus housing. 
・If the Sugimoto Campus or Morinomiya Campus is your main campus, please use the campus shuttle bus or public 
transportation. 
*The travel time from I-wing Nakamozu to Morinomiya Campus is about 1 hour. 
*If you use only the subway OSAKA METRO, you will need to pay about 340 yen for one-way transportation. In case of 
a commuter pass, about 12,000 yen per month is needed. 
*Depending on the route used, a one-way ticket may cost about 500 yen, while a commuter pass may require 16,000 
to 18,000 yen. 
*Exchange students are not eligible to purchase a “student commuter pass”. When purchasing a commuter pass, it 
must be a “regular commuter pass. 
・A new international student residence, OMU I-Dorm Sugimoto ( https://dormy-ac.com/page/omu-
ac/properties/kokusai-kouryu/), is expected to open on the Sugimoto Campus in April 2027. Detailed information 
regarding student dormitory will be provided together with the acceptance notification.

program. 
*A semi-annual transcript will not be issued for one-year acceptance. 
*If you need the grades by semester, students can check them on the student portal.

・OMU will apply for the COE on behalf of students to the Immigration Services Agency. 
*Necessary documents for application will be announced separately sent to the coordinator. 
*Issuance of COE is subject to review by the Immigration Services Agency. OMU cannot guarantee the issuance or  

【第4頁】
timing of COE. The COE may be delayed if the Immigration Services Agency takes a long time to review the 
application of COE. 
・Japanese nationals (including dual nationals) are not eligible to apply for COE since they enter the country as 
Japanese nationals. Information on procedures after entry into Japan will be provided separately. 
 
ISSUANCE OF LETTER OF ACCEPTANCE 
OMU will issue a Letter of Acceptance (PDF) as soon as the acceptance is decided. 
Please note that we cannot answer inquiries regarding the selection process. 
*The acceptance may be canceled if any false information is found in the application. 
 
VISA APPLICATION 
Please print out the LOA and COE and apply for the visa at the Japanese Embassy or Consulate.  
*It may take some time to apply for a visa, so please apply well in advance. 
*Some foreign embassies may require an appointment for visa application, so please check by yourself. 
*Please purchase your airline ticket after obtaining a visa. 
 
ORIENTATION FOR EXCHANGE STUDENTS 
・After arriving in Japan, an orientation regarding life in Japan will be provided. 
・Orientation includes an explanation of city hall procedures and campus services. 
・In addition, we will hold various orientations such as “Orientation for I-wing Nakamozu Residents”.  
 
SCHEDULE FROM APPLICATION TO END OF STUDY PERIOD（Reference） 
All times are in Japan time.  *The timing may be slightly earlier or later due to procedural reasons.

 ➇ Start of classes Early April 2027  
 ➈ Exam period *You can return home country after the exam. Late July - Early August 2027  
 ➉ Issuance of transcripts Early October 2027  
 
CONTACT  
国際戦略推進室 OMU Global Education TEL: +81-6-6167-1096  /  Email: gr-glo-inbound@omu.ac.jp 
【NOTE】Individual inquiries from students will not be accepted until the notification of acceptance is issued.  
All inquiries must be made through your home university's coordinator.

半期ごとの成績は本人が在籍中に学生ポータルにて確認できます。 
 
在留資格認定証明書（以下、COE） 
・COE の取得については、 申請時に申告された内容に基づき、大阪公立大学が出入国在留管理庁へ代理で申請します。  
※申請に必要な書類については大学担当者宛に別途案内します。 
※COE の発行は出入国在留管理庁の審査によるものです。大阪公立大学では、 COE の発行および発行時期について保証
できません。出入国在留管理庁の COE 発行に係る審査が⾧引いた場合は、送付が遅れる場合があります。  
・日本国籍をお持ちの方（二重国籍を含む）は、日本国籍で入国いただくため COE 申請の対象外となります。入国後の手
続きに関しては、別途案内します。 
 
受入許可証（Letter of Acceptance）の発行 
本学での受入許可の準備ができ次第、受入許可証（PDF）を発行します。 
なお、選考内容に関するお問い合わせにはお答えできませんので、ご了承ください。  
※受入許可証発行後であっても、申請内容の虚偽が発覚した場合、受け入れを取り消すことがあります。  
 
査証（ビザ）申請 
受入許可証（Letter of Acceptance）を印刷の上、電子在留資格認定証明書（COE）とともに在外公館へ査証申請をしてく
ださい。 
※ 査証（ビザ）申請に時間を要する場合がありますので、余裕を持って申請してください。 
※ 在外公館によっては、査証申請に予約が必要な場合がありますので、ご自身でご確認ください。 
※ 査証（ビザ）を取得した後に、航空券を購入してください。 
 

【第4頁】
交換留学生向けオリエンテーション 
・来日後に、日本での生活に関するオリエンテーションを実施します。  
・オリエンテーションでは、市役所手続きや学内サービスに関する説明を行います。  
・その他にも『I-wing なかもず入居者オリエンテーション』など各種オリエンテーションを実施します。 
 
申請から留学期間終了までのスケジュール（参考） 
すべて日本時間での時期となります。 ※手続きの都合で、時期が少し前後する場合があります。 
 内容 時期  
 ➀ 募集開始 2026 年 8 月下旬  
 ➁ ノミネーション締切 2026 年 10 月 1 日

国際戦略推進室 OMU Global Education TEL：+81-6-6167-1096   /   E-mail：gr-glo-inbound@omu.ac.jp

Overview
Under the Academic Course Access Program (ACAP), Science Tokyo waives the application, enrollment, and tuition fees of undergraduate (second-year or above) and graduate-level International Exchange Students from participating partner universities [
LIST of agreements
]. ACAP students are accepted for a period of one quarter to four quarters (a year) – for JASSO scholarship recipients, a period of two quarters (a semester) to four quarters (a year) – and are able to study alongside Science Tokyo students in regular courses offered on a quarter or semester basis.
*ACAP students are not permitted to take courses offered by the faculties/graduate schools of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Care Sciences.
Eligibility
Applicants must be enrolled at partner universities with which Science Tokyo has a tuition waiver agreement.
Those with student status at their home university, enrolled in the following programs at the time they start coursework at Science Tokyo:
・Doctoral program
・Master’s program
・Bachelor’s program (at least one year of study)*
*
Except for undergraduate students in their final year, an official Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT N1) result or equivalent document is required as students are supposed to take courses conducted in Japanese.
Applicants must carefully consider what they wish to study at Science Tokyo and prepare an ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet, which will be submitted to Science Tokyo through the partner university at the time of nomination.
Period of Study
From 1 quarter to 4 quarters (1 year)*
Start in April, June, October, or December (Starting month of each quarter)
*For JASSO scholarship recipients, the period of study must
start in either April or October and last from 2 quarters (a semester) to 4 quarters (a year)
.

1) Take course(s) offered at Science Tokyo (required): Mandated to take 6 classes (600 minutes) or more per week to maintain student visa status. *1 *2 *3 *4 and *6
(a)
Master's and doctoral students
can take
all courses offered by the graduate school
(conducted in English/Japanese).
(b)
Undergraduate students in their final year
can take courses for undergraduates (most of which are conducted in Japanese) and
courses for graduates also open to undergraduate-level international exchange students
(conducted in English).
(c)
Undergraduate students other than those in their final year
can take only
undergraduate courses mostly conducted in Japanese
. *5
(d) Students may take Japanese language courses at any level and are not allowed to take language classes other than Japanese.
2) Engage in at least one of the following activities (required):
(a) Take at least one of the following courses.
- Recommended Courses for International Exchange Students
And/or Japanese language courses at your level
(b) Participate in one of the monthly events organized by Science Tokyo.
*1
Course Numbers and Indicated Levels; 100-level, 200-level, 300-level: Undergraduate Level / 400-level, 500-level: Master's Level / 600-level: PhD Level
*2
Any courses conducted in English in the 100 and 200 levels cannot be taken.
*3
Before applying to this program, be sure to carefully check the information regarding course timetables and syllabi, and the list of courses from the previous year which details available graduate courses conducted in English, and confirm that a study plan matches course availability.
*4
There may be cases where your request for course registration is not permitted, as some courses have specific requirements for registration. In addition, some of the courses involving exercises/research training are not open to international exchange students.
*5
There are courses conducted in English in the 300-level, but those numbers are limited. If you are undergraduate students other than those in their final year and your Japanese language ability is not sufficient to take courses in Japanese, please confirm well in advance if you can achieve your study plan by taking the 300-level.
*6
ACAP students are not permitted to take courses offered by the faculties/graduate schools of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Care Sciences.

International Exchange Student (non-regular, non-degree-seeking student)

Application Procedures
Once you have decided to apply
Step 1. Contact the Student Exchange Officer (or equivalent) at your home university
ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet
ACAP applicants must be officially nominated to Science Tokyo by their home university, and Science Tokyo must be informed of the nomination BEFORE applicants are invited to apply online. At the time of nomination, the "ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet" prepared by each applicant should be submitted to Science Tokyo by their home university.
After receiving the official nomination from your home university, Science Tokyo will directly send you the necessary information for logging in to the online application form via email to you.
Step 2. Be assigned an Academic Supervisor at Science Tokyo
Science Tokyo's Schools
For all applicants, the Global Education Division will assign an ACAP Specialized Faculty member, selected from the applicant's desired department based on the ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet, to serve as their academic supervisor, and will notify the applicants of the result by email before application deadline. Applicants are NOT required to contact any faculty members at Science Tokyo directly.
Applicants applying to the Department of Architecture and Building Engineering are required to submit their Curriculum Vitae (CV) and portfolio via the online application form.
Currently, no applicants are accepted to the Department of Innovation Sciences.
After the application deadline, applicants are required to contact the assigned ACAP Specialized faculty member to confirm their acceptance and for an initial greeting.
Note that some Departments may exceed their capacity due to a high number of applicants and will be unable to accept additional students. In such cases, Science Tokyo will request the applicant to change their desired Department.
Step 3. Submit the required application materials online.
Three months to one month before enrollment
Step 4. The Certificate of Eligibility (COE) will be sent to you from the Global Education Division of Science Tokyo.
Two months to one month before enrollment
Step 5. Apply for your visa on your own with the COE which you have received.
Visa application processing time is expedited when you submit a COE with your visa application.

Enjoy your studies at Science Tokyo!

● Include the guidelines of the grading system in English.

3. Recommendation Letter (Free format)
● From your Academic Supervisor at your home university (Associate Professor or equivalent and above).

7. English Proficiency Test Score, or Equivalent Document
*Native speakers of English are exempt from this requirement.
● Submit the official test result (e.g. TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, Cambridge English, or Linguaskill).
● Or other official test with conversion tables to TOEFL, TOEIC, or IETS.
● For students who are not native speaker of English but enrolled in universities in English-speaking countries/regions (the UK, Philippines, Hong Kong, Singapore, USA, or Canada): An official document certifying that the primary language of instruction at your home university is English (Medium of Instruction certificate) is also acceptable.

●Required only for undergraduate students except for those in their final year
●Considering that students will be taking university-level courses conducted in Japanese, we expect them to have N1 level of JLPT.
9. Photograph
● Submit only ONE photo file. This will be used for both your COE and Student ID.
● Photo requirements: taken within the past 3 months, shows upper body and full face with a closed mouth (no smiling), plain background, and no caps/hats. The same photo as in your passport will not be accepted.
● JPEG format, resolution 300 dpi or higher, and file size less than 2MB, approximately 350 (H) × 290 (W) pixels.
● Refer to the
Immigration Services Agency's website
for facial expression and lighting standards ONLY. (Ignore the size requirement mentioned on their site.)
10. CV and Portfolio of your Previous Work
*Required only if the applicant’s major is
architecture
Important Notes on Language:
In principle, application documents must be written
in English only
. Documents written in a language other than English or Japanese must be accompanied by a certified English or Japanese translation. Translations should be certified by a public institution or the issuing university. Be sure to submit the original language version as well.

In addition to the above documents, submission of the following document(s) might be required.
1. Health Certificate for Infectious Diseases
International students whose registered enrollment period will be three months or longer are required to submit a health certificate for infectious disease control before your entrance date. Note that all expenses for this shall be borne by students. For more details, please refer to the following website:
Measures to help control infection for international students
2. Documents verifying your financial status in
English
) *Only if requested
Financial status verification* might be required as part of the application process for the Certificate of Eligibility (COE). You will be notified by the contact person at Science Tokyo in case the documents are needed to submit.
*For example, a bank statement (which verifies the available balance in the account) for you or your financial supporter; or a scholarship certificate (if any). If there is not an English version of these documents, you should attach a certified English translation with a signature of the translator and the date of translation.
Course Information for International Exchange Students
ACAP participants are mandated to take 6 classes (600 minutes) or more per week to maintain student visa status. All participants are assigned to one of Science Tokyo's Schools or Departments. In principle, they should plan their course of study mainly around courses offered in the Department to which they are assigned. However, not all courses offered at Science Tokyo are available for International Exchange Students. Final-year undergraduate students should refer to previously approved 400-level courses and carefully consider the courses they can take while studying abroad at Science Tokyo. Please refer to the document “
Science Tokyo Course Information to Help Develop Your Study Plan
.”
Housing
For students who have submitted a request to move into a Science Tokyo dormitory through the online application, the Global Education Division will request that the department in charge of university dormitories will allocate a room for them. (Students are not required to apply for dormitories individually.) Students will be notified by email 1 to 1.5 months prior to enrollment whether or not they will be able to move into the dormitory. In that case, please follow the instructions in the email. We do not accept changes of dormitories assigned to applicants. Note that not all incoming students will be assigned a dormitory room as room availability is limited.
Cost of Living in Tokyo/Japan
It depends on where you live, but you will need at least JPY 100,000 per month as of 2024.
References:
・Science Tokyo Dormitory fees: JPY 27,500-65,000 (plus a separate move-in fee)
・Bottle of water: JPY 100-150
・Lunch at cafeteria at Science Tokyo: JPY 400-600
・Lunch at café or restaurant in Tokyo: JPY 1,000-1,500

Notified by Science Tokyo by the end of February (for admission in April) or August (for admission in October)
*1
The number of JASSO scholarship recipients is limited, and recipient selection will be made by Science Tokyo.
*2
Students receiving more than JPY 80,000 per month in total from other scholarships to study in Japan are ineligible for this scholarship. Also, some scholarship foundations do not allow their recipients to receive a stipend from another scholarship foundation. Please confirm that receipt of a JASSO scholarship WILL NOT jeopardize funding which you already receive from another scholarship foundation.

Before beginning the online application process, applicants are required to contact a desired academic supervisor at Science Tokyo directly, and obtain approval from him/her. On the online application form, applicants need to submit evidence such as an email message or a letter indicating that the Science Tokyo professor agrees to be the applicant’s academic supervisor.
Please note that only professors, associate professors and lecturers are eligible to be academic supervisors. (Assistant professors may or may not be qualified. Please consult with us in advance.)
YSEP students cannot be accepted by the faculties/graduate schools of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Care Sciences.
For those who apply for the
Department of Architecture and Building Engineering,
this process is done by the Global Education Division on their behalf, and they are not allowed to contact their desired supervisors directly. Instead, applicants are required to submit their CV and portfolio via the online application form.
Those applying for the

should contact the Global Education Division in advance. Our contact information can be found at the end of this document.

Science Tokyo will apply on behalf of applicants for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) after they complete the application procedures. To be completed online. Science Tokyo will directly send you the necessary information for logging in to the online application form via email to you.
2. Official Transcript in English
● Include the guidelines of the grading system in English.
● Submit transcripts for at least the last academic year.
● Science Tokyo reserves the right to verify the authenticity of your transcript.
3. Recommendation Letter (Free format)
● From your Academic Supervisor at your home university (Associate Professor or equivalent and above).
● Language teachers cannot be regarded as academic supervisors.
4. Verification of Student Status at Home University
● Certify your student status at your home university while at Science Tokyo.

7. English Proficiency Test Score, or Equivalent Document
*Native speakers of English are exempt from this requirement.
● Submit the official test result (e.g. TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, Cambridge English, or Linguaskill).
● Or other official test with conversion tables to TOEFL, TOEIC, or IETS.
● For students who are not native speaker of English but enrolled in universities in English-speaking countries/regions (the UK, Philippines, Hong Kong, Singapore, USA, or Canada): An official document certifying that the primary language of instruction at your home university is English (Medium of Instruction certificate) is also acceptable.
8. Photograph for COE Application and Student ID
● Submit only ONE photo file. This will be used for both your COE and Student ID.
● Photo requirements: taken within the past 3 months, shows upper body and full face with a closed mouth (no smiling), plain background, and no caps/hats. The same photo as in your passport will not be accepted.
● JPEG format, resolution 300 dpi or higher, and file size less than 2MB, approximately 350 (H) × 290 (W) pixels.

Course Information for International Exchange Students

Non-degree Programs

A variety of programs are available for non-regular students, including programs for students from partner universities and programs for students from other universities. Tokyo Tech also offers various learning opportunities such as those for research students and non-degree students.
International Exchange Students
Students from the institue’s partner universities who would like to study at Tokyo Tech as non-regular students for up to one year may apply to Tokyo Tech as International Exchange Students.
For more information
Overseas Partner Universities
From Partner Universities with Institutional-Level Agreement (Tuition Waiver)
Young Science and Engineering Researchers Program (YSEP)
YSEP is offered as a research-oriented program. Participants conduct research activities under the guidance of an academic supervisor at Tokyo Tech.
- Eligibility: Undergraduate- and graduate-level students
- Period of Stay: From 5 months to 1 year
Academic Course Access Program (ACAP)
ACAP is offered as a course-oriented program. Participants take courses offered at Tokyo tech.
- Eligibility: Undergraduate- and graduate-level students
- Period of Stay: From 1 quarter to 4 quarters (1 year)
From Partner Universities with Institutional-Level Agreement (with Tuition and Fee Payment)
International Exchange Student (Other Participants)
International Exchange Students (Other Participants) is for students from partner universities, provided they pay tuition and fees to Tokyo Tech.
- Eligibility: Undergraduate- and graduate-level students
- Period of Stay: From 1 month to 1 year
From Designated Partner Universities
CAMPUS Asia
CAMPUS Asia is a joint education and research program with Tsinghua University and KAIST.
- Eligibility: Fourth-year undergraduate- and graduate-level students
- Period of Stay: Refer to program website
CAMPUS Asia website
Summer Program
The Summer Program is a research-oriented program for undergraduate and graduate students.
- Eligibility: Undergraduate- and graduate-level students
- Period of Stay: June to August (10 weeks)
Winter Program
The Winter Program conducts the virtual student-exchange program Bringing Ideas in Remote Discussion (BIRD).
- Eligibility: Current undergraduate and graduate students at The University of Melbourne
- Program Period: February (10 days)
From Partner Universities with School-Level Agreement (Tuition Waiver)
Department Exchange Programs
Each department offers a variety of programs. Eligibility and length of study vary by program.
- Eligibility: Undergraduate- and graduate-level students
- Period of Stay: From 1 month to 1 year
After you are accepted to Tokyo Tech
Course Information for International Exchange Students
Course information for International Exchange Students who plan to register for courses at Tokyo Tech
International Visiting Students (from Non-partner Universities)
Students from non-partner universities can engage in study and research at Tokyo Tech as International Visiting Students.
For more information
Overseas Partner Universities
International Visiting Students
International Visiting Students are accepted from non-partner universities, provided they pay tuition and fees to Tokyo Tech.
- Eligibility: Undergraduate- and graduate-level students
- Period of Stay: From 1 month to 1 year
International Exchange/Visiting Students FAQ
FAQ
Answers to frequently asked questions about International Exchange/Visiting Students are included on the FAQ page.
Graduate Research Students
Tokyo Tech accepts non-regular students who wish to conduct research under the guidance of Tokyo Tech faculty members (academic supervisors) as Research Students. Given that research is the purpose of admission, proof of sufficient scholastic ability to conduct research is a prerequisite for acceptance. Prospective applicants should contact the faculty member whom they wish to supervise their research and receive that professor's consent before filing an application. In principle, Research Students cannot take classes. However, should an academic supervisor find it necessary for a Research Student to take a course, attending may be possible with approval from the course instructor.
Graduate Research Students (Privately Funded)
Privately funded international students who enroll as Research Students
- Eligibility: Undergraduates, graduates, or prospective graduates
- Period of Stay 6 months or 1 year
Non-degree Students
The non-degree student system makes it possible for Tokyo Tech to meet the needs of different types of student, including mid-career professionals, by allowing them to acquire credit for taking regular university courses.
Non-degree Students
- Study in bachelor's level courses
Applicants must have completed high school-level education.
- Study in graduate-level courses
Applicants must have completed a level of education equivalent to that of a bachelor's degree.

Dormitories and other accommodation
Science Tokyo students live in various housing options including university dormitories, dormitories operated by external organizations, private apartments, and shared houses. Find the housing that suits you for a fulfilling student life.
* Monthly dormitory fees as of October 2024. These may change in the future.
About Dormitories
Choose a dormitory that is convenient for commuting to your main campus. Check the dormitory locations, facilities, and application conditions from the links below.
Science Tokyo Dormitories for Students
Recommended campuses:
Ookayama Campus, Suzukakedai Campus, Yushima Campus
Dormitories Recommended by Science Tokyo
Dormitories operated by external organizations (Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO) dormitories and private company dormitories) for which students can apply with Science Tokyo recommendation.
Finding private apartments and shared houses
Many students live in private apartments or shared houses. Visit real estate agencies in the area where you want to live or search for properties on the internet, and start your preparations early.
Finding housing
We introduce services and companies that support your house hunting.
Finding through housing support
Science Tokyo Housing Support assists international students and researchers looking for accommodation.We provide various information on house hunting sites, companies, and agencies.

About guarantor companies for international students
In Japan, most apartment rental contracts require a co-signer. If international students cannot find a financially stable co-signer in Japan, they should use a guarantor company that acts as a co-signer.

Measures to help control infection for international students
Tweet
Measures to help control infection for international students
Tweet
To support student health and infectious disease prevention, Institute of Science Tokyo requires all incoming international students, both degree-seeking and non-degree-seeking, to submit a health certificate and strongly recommends participation in the annual medical checkup.
Who should submit?
International students who have been admitted to the university and will be enrolled for three months or longer, including those transferring from universities, colleges of technology, or Japanese language schools in Japan.
*Not applicable to currently enrolled international students who were enrolled at Science Tokyo in the previous year and have already submitted Health Certificate Parts I and II.
Deadline
The required documents must be submitted before the enrollment date at Science Tokyo, or within three months prior to the planned date of arrival in Japan if arrival is after enrollment.
Examples:
Enrollment date: April 1 → Deadline: March 31
Enrollment date: October 1 → Deadline: September 30
Health Certificate
Download the form from the link below and have a physician at a medical institution in your home country complete it in English or Japanese within three months prior to your enrollment date at Science Tokyo (or your planned date of arrival in Japan, if you will arrive after enrollment).
Health-Certificate-Part1.pdf
Health-Certificate-Part2.pdf
Part I: Tuberculosis (TB) Screening
Must be submitted by international students
falling under 1. or 2. below.
They must undergo an Interferon Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) test and have a physician complete the form.
1. Individuals who were born in or stayed long term (more than 6 months) in
countries or territories that have a high incidence of active TB.
2. Individuals who have had close contact with persons known or suspected to have active TB.
Part II: Certificate of Vaccinations
Must be submitted by
ALL
international students. They must have a physician complete the form.
Important:
If you are unable to complete the required vaccinations before enrollment, receive the first dose in your home country and upload the record. Complete the remaining dose(s) after arriving in Japan and email proof of vaccination to the address below.
Please refer to the list of medical institutions below if you plan to be vaccinated in Japan.
See clinics where vaccinations are availablen in Japan.
Items to Be Included in the Health Certificate
Part Ⅰ:  Interferon Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) results (blood test)
Individuals from countries with a high incidence of tuberculosis (see link below)
are required to undergo an IGRA test within three months prior to their arrival in Japan.
Countries or territories that have a high incidence of active TB
Part Ⅱ:  Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPDs)
Required for
All International Students
1. Measles, Mumps, Rubella, and Varicella
Provide one of the following for each disease:
● Antibody titer test result (with laboratory report)
● Record of two vaccine doses (with vaccination dates)
● History of infection (with documented date of diagnosis)
Notes:
・If your antibody test result is
negative or indeterminate
, you must consult a physician or travel clinic
and receive vaccination.
・Vaccinations without documentation will be considered
not received.
・ Science Tokyo recommends
completion of the standard vaccination schedule (two doses for each vaccine).
2. Tetanus
● Provide a record of tetanus vaccination received within the past 10 years.
● If you have not been vaccinated within the past 10 years, receive a tetanus-containing vaccine
(e.g., Tetanus Toxoid, Tdap, or Td).
● Antibody titer test results are not accepted in place of vaccination records.
● Tetanus Immune Globulin (TIG) is not accepted. A tetanus vaccine is required.
How to Submit the Health Certificate
Submit the health certificate from
this
system.
Please prepare all required documents before entering any information into the online system.  If you are unable to submit the documents through the online system, please contact us at the email address below.
Personal Information Protection
The collected personal information will be managed in compliance with all the laws and regulations regarding personal information for all students at Science Tokyo, and will not be used for any purposes other than those indicated in
the Policy on Protecting the Privacy of Students, Faculty, and Staff at the Health Support Center
Frequently Asked Questions
1. Is there a designated medical institution for the health certificate?
No. It is acceptable as long as it is completed in either English or Japanese by a physician.
2. Does the health certificate have to be completed in English, including the name and address of the medical institution?
The health certificate, including the name and address of the medical institution, must be completed either in Japanese or English.
3. Does the health certificate have to be stamped with a seal of the medical institution?
The health certificate should either be signed by the physician or stamped by the medical institution.
4. Is there financial assistance for vaccine shots in Japan?
No. You are responsible for the expenses.Also note that Japanese health insurance does not cover vaccinations.
5. Can I be exempt from submitting the health certificate?
No, it’s mandatory. If this is not followed, your academic supervisor will be notified.
6. I was a student at  Science Tokyo in the past( or I am a newly enrolled internal student)and have stayed in Japan since then.  Do I need to submit the health certificate?
Only if you did not submit it when you were previously enrolled.
7. In place of the IGRA test (blood test) for Part I, can I use the PPD test (tuberculin test) results?
The IGRA test is highly recommended as the PPD test is prone to false-positive and false-negative results. Only under the condition that there is no local medical institution providing an IGRA test AND you have never had a BCG(vaccination for TB)in the past, you may use PPD test result.
8. TB screening tests are pricey in my country. In Japan, is there financial assistance for students, or are there options that are less expensive?
No. We understand that tests are expensive. However, we ask for your cooperation in implementing measures to help control infection.
If IGRA testing is applicable to you, please undergo a test (costing about 10,000 yen in Japan) and submit a completed Part I form.
9. What should I do if I don’t have records?
If you do not have the records of immunization, do either A or B below.
A.　Take an antibody test and submit the lab report. If the antibody titer is below the acceptable level, consult the doctor for an additional shot.
B.　Get vaccinated for MMR, varicella, and tetanus.
For MMR and varicella, you should be vaccinated twice. If you only have one record of vaccination, you should also take the titer test at least two months after the previous vaccination and submit the lab report with PartⅡ.
Vaccination for tetanus must be done within the past 10 years.  If not, a booster is required.
10. I have my childhood vaccination record proving that required vaccinations have been completed. Can I skip Part II if I submit a copy of the record?
No. Have your physician complete Part II based on your vaccination record. If not, take the titer tests prove that you have immunity and complete the document.
11. I cannot get the required vaccination in my country.
Get vaccinated upon arrival in Japan. Enter “to be vaccinated upon arrival in Japan” in the Part II form, and upload the form online. Upon vaccination after your arrival, submit a receipt from the clinic via emai to notify the Healthcare Center Center that you have completed the vaccination.
12. Vaccination for tetanus is not available in my country.
Get vaccinated with Tetanus Diphtheria and Pertussis vaccines (Tdap or DTP), which also provide you with protection against Pertussis (whooping cough).  If neither of the vaccinations are available, follow the instructions written in  Q.11
13.  I am planning to receive the second dose of the vaccine in Japan but I received/will receive the first one in another country . My proof of vaccination is written in a language other than Japanese or English. Will I be able to use this?
No, if you get the first dose of the vaccine in another country, have the doctor fill out PartⅡ in English and upload the document online. After you get your second shot in Japan, follow the instruction written in Q.11.
14. I’ve finished all the vaccine shots. Do I still need to undergo an immune titer test for Part II?
If you only have one shot for MMR and for varicella, you need to take the antibody tests to confirm that you are immuned(positive) and submit the lab report as well. If the lab report is either negative or equivocal, you must consult the doctor for an additional shot.
15. Does Science Tokyo have specific recommendations for vaccine brands?
No. Consult your physician and do as advised.
16. Does Science Tokyo make arrangements for me to receive vaccine shots in Japan?
No. You need to do it by yourself.  Refer to 『travel-clinics.pdf』of this page for clinics available in Japan.
Contact
Student Healthcare Center at Ookayama
Institute of Science Tokyo
HE-1,2-12-1 Ookayama, Meguro-ku
Tokyo 152-8550 Japan
Tel:
+81-3-5734-2065
Email: info_health@shc.isct.ac.jp
Note: In order to avoid discrepancies in the communication of information, we will not be able respond to inquiries from proxies.

title: 東京科學大學：東京科學官方：dorm-faq（116適用性待查）
text:
【網頁／無PDF頁碼】
Frequently Asked Questions
Frequently asked questions about applying for a student dormitory and living in a dormitory are listed below. Please read them before you apply.
About dormitory applications
Expand all
Q
I'd like to enter Tokyo Tech next spring and stay in a student dormitory. When do applications open?
A
We start accepting online applications from mid-January.
Q
Can I apply before the release of the entrance exam results?
A
Yes. However, you’ll lose your eligibility if you fail the exam.
Q
I’d like to secure a room in a dormitory in February, before the entrance exam results in March. Is that possible if I pay rent?
A
Not allowed. You can move in after the move-in date.
Q
Can I apply for more than one dormitory and indicate my first choice, second choice, etc.?
A
Applications will only be accepted for one dormitory. However, if you are unable to move into the dormitory you have applied for, we may be able to offer you another dormitory if one is available.
Q
Could my application be rejected? What’s the ratio of applications for dormitories?
A
Selection will be by lottery if the number of applications exceeds capacity.
The ratio of applications differs every year, depending on the dormitory.
Q
If my application is successful, can I choose my room? Can I request a room change after moving in?
A
You can’t choose your room or roommates, and room change requests are not accepted.
Q
Is there a charge for cancellation?
A
No cancellation fee will be charged.
Q
Will the initial fee be refunded when I leave?
A
The initial fee is not refundable.
Q
Can I view rooms before applying?
A
A Yes. Please contact the Student Support Division.
(No viewing available for Suzukakedai House and Minami-Tsukushino House)
Q
Can I keep my room while on a leave of absence or studying abroad? If yes, will I be charged rent?
A
Please inquire separately as it depends on the period and circumstances.
Q
What is the “reservation number” printed on my application form?
A
It’s a number for students enrolling in certain specified programs.
About dormitory life
Expand all
Q
Is there a curfew?
A
No curfew.
Q
Can my friends visit me in my room?
A
In principle, only residents are allowed to enter private rooms. Access to common areas is handled differently in each dormitory, so please inquire for details.
Q
May friends stay overnight?
A
Non-residents are not allowed to stay overnight.
Q
Are meals provided?
A
No, the dormitories aren’t catered.
Q
Is there a TV in the dormitory? If not, can I bring my own?
A
Private rooms are not equipped with a TV, but some dormitories have common rooms with one. Please consult us if you would like to bring your own.
Q
Can I access the internet in my room?
A
Internet service is available in the dormitory. No application is required.
Q
Is bedding provided?
A
Those in other dormitories have only a mattress. Please bring your own bedding set and linen, or purchase them from our supplier at a discount rate. (No purchasing available for Suzukakedai House and Minami-Tsukushino House)
Q
How do I pay the rent?
A
Payment methods differ depending on the dormitory. We’ll explain the relevant procedure to each student well before their residency starts.
Minamishinagawa House
Expand all
Q
Is the Minami-Shinagawa House located within cycling distance of the campus?
A
Yes. Some residents commute by bicycle.
Q
What appliances are provided in residential units?
A
There is a refrigerator, microwave.
Senzokuike House
Expand all
Q
Can I have a specific address?
A
Only if you’ve been assigned a room. Please contact us if you would like to view the facility.
Q
Can my friends visit me in the house?
A
Female visitors are allowed to visit, but may only enter the dining room and lounge.
Q
I’d like to ask my father to help me move in/out. Can he enter the dormitory?
A
He’ll be allowed to enter the dining room and lounge on the first floor only. Please follow the rules about visitors.
Midorigaoka House
Expand all
Q
Are undergraduate students accepted?
A
No, the Midorigaoka House is exclusively for graduate students.
Nagatsuta House
Expand all
Q
Is there a shuttle bus to the campus?
A
Yes, there’s a free shuttle bus that for only Nagatsuta House residents  between the dormitory and Suzukakedai Campus — three times in the morning and evening. It takes about 10 minutes.
Unfortunately, Nagatsuta House residents are not allowed to ride bicycles to school.
Komaba Dormiory, Shofu  Dormiory and Umegaoka Dormiory
Expand all
Q
I’m a new international student. Can I apply for an international dormitory?
A
New international students and exchange students who have received an invitation to move in from the Student Support Division and have a reservation number may apply.
Q
How can I get a reservation number?
A
If you have a reservation number, yes. We send information about dormitories along with a reservation number to eligible international students.
Q
Can Japanese students reside in the dormitory?
A
Only those assigned as dormitory tutors will be permitted and may be able to move in when recruited.
Contact
Student Support Division (Dormitory)
Email
dormitory.se@adm.isct.ac.jp

2026/01/15 
 
CALL FOR APPLICATION  
TOKYO INTERNATIONAL EXCHANGE CENTER (TIEC)  
<Nomination System 2026 > 
 
1. Application Requirements for international students: 
(1) Current graduate students with outstanding study record, who have student visa status, and can commute 
from the TIEC to campus. Prospective students who are admitted by Science Tokyo are also eligible to 
apply. (They may move-in 30 days prior to the enrollment.) (Please submit a photocopy of acceptance 
letter with your application form.) 
* No qualification for those who are taking, or will take a leave of absence. 
* No qualification for those who have extended or extend their term of study. 
(2) Students who participate in exchange programs (graduate course level) held by Institute of Science Tokyo 
for more than 30 days. Those students who don’t have student visa status are also eligible to apply. 
(3) Residence period is within 1 year (It is extendable up to 3 years if it is within the term of study and 
JASSO approves it). JASSO approves it after review about applicants’ attendance to TIEC events, and their 
behavior while living in TIEC. 
If the term of study is until August 2026, the residence period ends by August 25, 2026. If the term of study 
is until September 2026, the residence period ends by September 25, 2026. If the term of study is until 
March 2027, the residence period ends by March 25, 2027. 
(4) As room assignments are made through university recommendation, we kindly ask that you refrain 
from canceling after receiving approval for residence. Please take this into careful consideration 
when submitting your application.   
 
2. Document Required: 
(1) Application for Tokyo International Exchange Center (Form 1)   
(2) The proposal for implementation / participation of exchange activities at TIEC (Form 3)  
(3) Application for Tokyo International Exchange Center (Form 14-1)   
(4) Pledge for Science Tokyo 
(5) A photocopy of Student ID card 
*If you were a new student, you may submit the photocopy of the letter of acceptance or the admission permit, instead of Student ID card. 
(6) A photocopy of Passport (including cohabitants/ *pages of photo, visa and showing the landing permit date) 
(7) A photocopy of Residence card (including cohabitants / *both sides.) 
(8) (Only for applicants of Hall C or D) Certificate of Residence (住民票) issued within three months (for 
cohabitants) or official certificate shows relationship between you and your cohabitants, written in English or 
Japanese.

2026/01/15

scanned copy of Form14, Pledge, and other documents.

International student guide
This guide compiles necessary and useful information for international students regarding life in Japan and studying at Science Tokyo. There are unique systems and procedures specifically for international students, so when you're in doubt or trouble, first use this guide to collect the information you need.
International student guide
This international student guide contains important information for your studies at Science Tokyo. Since there are certain systems and procedures specific to international students, please refer to it as needed.
The guide is only available in English.
Table of contents
1. Residence Status and Registration Procedures
2. Visa Consulting Service
3. Japanese Health and Social Insurance Systems
4．Student Insurance
5. Medical Checkup
6．Counseling and Support System
7．Certifications
8．Administrative Divisions in Charge of Student Affairs
9. Accommodations
10．Commuter Passes and Student Discounts
11．Inviting Family Members to Japan
12．Use of the Libraries
13. Career Support

16. Science Tokyo Tsubame Scholarship for Doctoral Students
17．Useful Information
1. Residence Status and Registration Procedures
1.1 Residence Card
1.2 Registration of Address Information
1.3 Change in Information on the Residence Card Other than Place of Residence
1.4 Social Security and Tax Number (Individual Number)
1.5 Procedures to Be Taken before Traveling Overseas from Japan
1.6 When Taking a Leave of Absence
1.7 When Studying Abroad
1.8 When Undertaking an Internship in/outside Japan
1.9 When Graduating from Science Tokyo/ Completing a Degree Program
1.10 When Withdrawing/ Being Expelled from Science Tokyo
1.11 Extension of Period of Stay
1.12 Applying for Permission to Engage in Activity Other than That Permitted under the Status of Residence Previously Granted
1.1 Residence Card
A residence card is issued at the port of entry to persons entering Japan who have been granted residence status with a period of stay of three or more months. Please carry your residence card with you at all times.
1.2 Registration of Address Information
(1) Notification of Place of Residence (registration of residence)
After entering Japan, international students are required to report their place of residence to local municipal offices without delay. Submit a Notification of Place of Residence to the office for registration of your residency within 14 days after moving in.
(2) Procedures to Be Taken When Changing Residence
a. Notify the local municipal or ward office
Whenever you move to a new residence, you are required to notify your local municipal or ward office of the change of address within 14 days after moving in.
b. Notify the Student Division and the Student Support Division
Science and engineering students
Bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral students:
Please change your address on the website (Web System for Students and Faculty).
Additionally, please bring your residence card with the new address to Student Support Division for scanning.
Research Students, International Exchange Students, International Visiting Students, Japanese Intensive Course Students:
Please bring your residence card with the new address to Student Support Division for scanning.
Medical and dental sciences students
Undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and research students:
Please submit a copy of both sides of your updated residence card that lists the new address to the Student Support Division at Yushima Campus via the following link:
- Reporting Your Residence Status "Student"
c. Change the address registered on your National Health Insurance Card.
Once you have changed your address, you can no longer use the National Health Insurance Card issued with your former address. To change the address, complete the required procedures at the local municipal or ward office for your new address without delay. Please bring your old National Health Insurance Card with you.
d. Change the address registered on your bank account.
Please notify your bank of any change of address. Bring your bankbook to the bank where it was issued and have the address updated. If scholarship recipients fail to do so, their scholarships may not be credited appropriately.
e. Notify the post office.
To receive letters and mail addressed to your former address at your new place, request a mail forwarding service at a post office. Fill in and submit the prescribed form which is available at any post office, and mail will be forwarded to your new address for up to one year. Note that mail cannot be forwarded to overseas addresses; forwarding addresses must be in Japan. Please also note that forwarded mail will take longer to reach you than normal, since it takes some time to redirect mail to a different address.
1.3 Change in Information on the Residence Card Other than Place of Residence
If there is any change in the information on the residence card other than the address (e.g., name, date of birth, sex, nationality/region) or termination of the “Student” status of residence (e.g., graduation, withdrawal, etc.), mid-to-long-term residents must report it to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of the change. Bring your residence card to the nearest office and complete the necessary procedures. Failing to do so may result in penalties or revocation of status of residence. Once the necessary procedures are completed, a new residence card will be issued.
After receiving your new residence card with the updated information, please notify the Student Support Division.
1.4 Social Security and Tax Number (Individual Number)
In accordance with the Social Security and Tax Number System (My Number System), all registered residents of Japan are issued a twelve-digit individual number. This number will be required for various types of administrative procedures, including social security and tax procedures, as well as disaster countermeasures. This number is very important for managing personal information, so please do not throw it away or show it to other persons. It is valid for life. The same number will be issued when leaving and re-entering Japan.
1.5 Procedures to Be Taken before Traveling Overseas from Japan
Science and engineering students
Notify the Global Education Division.
Regular students
Please submit an “Overseas Travel Notice” via Rakrak WF II. For more information, please visit the following website.
Procedures for Study Abroad and Other Overseas Travel
Non-regular students
Please submit an “Overseas Travel Notice” via Microsoft Forms using the link below.
- International exchange students and international visiting students
- Non-regular students who are not international exchange or visiting students
Medical and dental sciences students
Notify the Student Support Division.
All students
Please submit a “Temporary Leave Notice” via Microsoft Forms using the link below here:
Temporary Leave Notice
Whenever you travel outside Japan (including travel for vacations and travel to your home country), please ensure that you have travel insurance.
1.6 When Taking a Leave of Absence
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to take a leave of absence.
If you take a leave of absence, you cannot remain in Japan under "Student" status, nor are you allowed to work part-time. You must leave Japan promptly or change to an appropriate residence status if you wish to stay.
If you are going to take a leave of absence for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport. You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to resume studying at Science Tokyo. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
1.7 When Studying Abroad
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to study abroad.
If you are going to study abroad for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to re-enter Japan. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
1.8 When Undertaking an Internship in/outside Japan
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to undertake internships.
If you undertake an internship abroad for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to re-enter Japan. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
If you are going to undertake an internship in Japan, see the Immigration Services Agency's website and apply for permission as necessary.
For those wishing to apply for an internship | Immigration Services Agency
1.9 When Graduating from Science Tokyo/ Completing a Degree Program
The "Student" status is only valid during your period of enrollment at Science Tokyo. After graduation or completion, you must leave Japan promptly, even if your period of stay still remains valid. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
If your period of stay includes extra time beyond your enrollment for departure preparation, (i.e., if your residence period is significantly longer than your period of enrollment), you cannot change to "Temporary visitor" status for the purpose of such preparation.
If you plan to stay in Japan after graduation/completion, you must change to an appropriate status (see below for examples) and submit a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)" to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of graduation/completion, unless you continue your studies at Science Tokyo.
Immigration Services Agency website for a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)"
If you are planning to start work: contact the company where you have received a job offer (Naitei) and change your status to "Working."
If you already have a job offer (Naitei) from a company and want to stay in Japan until your job starts: contact the company and change your status to "Designated Activities (Naitei Taiki)."
If you want to continue job hunting (regular students only): contact the Student Support Division and apply for a change of status to "Designated Activities (Job Hunting)."
If you have a letter of acceptance to a graduate school and want to stay until the date of enrollment: contact the Student Support Division and apply for a change of status to "Designated Activities (Shingaku Taiki)."
1.10 When Withdrawing/ Being Expelled from Science Tokyo
If you withdraw or are expelled from Science Tokyo, you cannot remain in Japan under "Student" status and must leave Japan promptly. When departing, please return your residence card at the airport.
If you plan to stay in Japan to enroll at another university or to work in Japan, please check your status with your new university or company. You must also submit a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)" to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of the date of withdrawal/expulsion.
Immigration Services Agency website for a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)"
1.11 Extension of Period of Stay
Undergraduate international students who have acquired less than 25 credits over the past year may not be granted permission to renew their period of stay. (For medical and dental science students, this applies to those who have not acquired the required credits for advancement to the next academic year.)
For details, refer to the Science Tokyo website
Find the application procedures and necessary documents for extending your stay or changing your status of residence. Please check the relevant contact points according to your field below.
Science and engineering students
Students affiliated with the Ookayama Campus:
Open Science Tokyo Slack
Students affiliated with the Yokohama Campus:
Open Science Tokyo Slack
Medical and dental sciences students
Visit website
1.12 Applying for Permission to Engage in Activity Other than That Permitted under the Status of Residence Previously Granted
If international students must find a part-time job to pay for their studies or other expenses, they must receive permission to engage in activity other than that permitted under the status of residence previously granted (“Extra-status Activity”) by following the procedures prescribed by the Ministry of Justice. International students are allowed to work up to 28 hours per week (up to 8 hours per day during extended breaks).
If you engage in a part-time job without obtaining permission, your current visa status may be revoked. Furthermore, you may not apply for permission for certain types of jobs (those related to the adult entertainment industry, cleaning duties in pachinko parlors, etc.). Note that TAs, RAs, and tutors employed by Science Tokyo do not need to obtain this permission.
Required Documents
Application Form
The application form can be downloaded from the following link:
APPLICATION FOR PERMISSION TO ENGAGE IN ACTIVITY OTHER THAN THAT PERMITTED UNDER THE STATUS OF RESIDENCE PREVIOUSLY GRANTED
Passport (original)
Residence card (original)
Where to Apply
Applicants can submit the documents either to the Visa Consulting Service staff or directly to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau.
If you use the Visa Consulting Service, bring a copy of your passport and Residence Card with you.
Application Processing Time
Two weeks to one month
2. Visa Consulting Service
Science Tokyo has launched the Immigration and Visa Consulting Service to support international students and researchers with application procedures that concern international residents. On designated days, professionals from a law office will be available at the Student Support Division at Ookayama Campus and Yokohama Campus (Suzukake Hall, H1, H2 Bldg., Floor 2) and at the Yushima Student Support Office at Yushima Campus (Building 5, Floor 3). We invite you to make use of this service at your convenience.
Through this service, you no longer need to go to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau for most types of applications. Consultation is free of charge, but you will need to pay a commission if you use the application service. You are required to make a reservation in advance, and to bring your student ID card every time you use this service. (Your student visa must be valid for at least another 2 weeks.)
Details of when the service is available will be announced at:
Immigration & Visa Consulting Service
Reservation page

Certificate of Eligibility (Student, Researcher, Professor, Dependent)

3. Japanese Health and Social Insurance Systems
3.1 Join the National Health Insurance System
3.2 Apply for National Pension Contribution Special Payment System for Students
3.1 Join the National Health Insurance System
International students planning to reside in Japan for more than three months are required to join the National Health Insurance System at their local municipal or ward office. Although students must pay insurance premiums, they will only have to pay 30% of medical expenses while under the health insurance coverage.
Insurance premiums differ according to the ward or city, but the basic amount is approximately JPY 30,000 per year. If your annual income is low, you may be entitled to a reduction by applying at your local municipal or ward office, which must be done every year. Typically, the reduced premium is approximately JPY 10,000 per year, but it varies depending on the municipality or ward.
Note: Reimbursement for High-Cost Medical Care Payments
If your share of medical expenses incurred in a single calendar month exceeds a certain threshold, you may be eligible for reimbursement for high-cost medical care payments. The threshold varies depending on factors related to your income and age, but for most people, it is around JPY 35,400. To apply, submit an application to your local municipal office, attaching your National Health Insurance Card, receipts issued by the hospitals or pharmacies, and a detailed statement of medical expenses. Application reviews typically take two to three months, but processing times can vary. For details, consult the municipal office or ward office in your area.
3.2 Apply for National Pension Contribution Special Payment System for Students
All people between the ages of 20 and 59 who have a registered address in Japan must be covered by the National Pension system and must pay contributions, regardless of nationality or length of stay. If your income in Japan from the previous year is equal to or less than a specified amount, you may apply for the Special Payment System for Students to request a postponement of contribution payments. You need to file an application for each year with the municipal or ward office. By undergoing this procedure, you establish valid coverage periods that count toward the eligibility requirements for receiving future old-age pension benefits, as well as current benefits if you are accidentally injured and become disabled. For details, visit the Japan Pension Service website, where a sample of the application is available in English.
For details
4．Student Insurance
- Personal Accident Insurance for Students Pursuing Education and Research (Gakkensai)
- Personal Liability Insurance for Students (Futaibaiseki, Gakkenbai, or Igakubai)
All Science Tokyo students are expected to purchase certain insurance policies.
Personal Accident Insurance for Students Pursuing Education and Research (Gakkensai) provides financial assistance to students injured in accidents/disasters during studies, lab work, extracurricular activities, or commuting to or from campus.
Personal Liability Insurance for Students (Gakkenbai, Futaibaiseki Course A) covers costs for property damage or injuries to third parties resulting from accidents during most official Science Tokyo activities.
Science and engineering students are required to enroll in Gakkensai and Gakkenbai.
Medical and dental sciences undergraduate students
are required to enroll in Gakkensai. Depending on your affiliated school, you may also have to enroll in an additional liability insurance policy that covers accidents during medical or clinical training known as Igakubai (Futaibaiseki Course C).

4.4 Enrolling in the Insurance
Science and engineering student
Please use the e-shiharai service to pay your insurance premium during enrollment. If you enroll without paying, promptly collect a payment slip from the Student Support Division and pay the premium. Students advancing to the next degree level or changing programs (e.g., from a master's program to a doctoral program, or from a research student program to a master's program) must reapply.
Medical and dental sciences students
Pay insurance premiums to the bank account designated by Science Tokyo. Students who are advancing to a higher degree or changing programs (such as from a master’s to a doctorate, or from being a researcher to becoming a master’s student) need to go through the application procedure again. As a general rule, students must enroll in the insurance before starting their studies at Science Tokyo. Insurance premium payments are not accepted via overseas remittance, and international students are required to complete payment and necessary procedures immediately after arriving in Japan.

Science and engineering students
Should you be involved in any of the abovementioned accidents, please notify the Student

Please email the Student Support Division (studentinsurance.md(at)adm.isct.ac.jp).
4.6 Car Insurance
All cars and motorcycles must be covered by the compulsory automobile liability insurance. As
it only covers compensation for third parties for bodily injury in the case of an accident and does
not cover property damage or injury to the driver, it is highly recommended that voluntary
automobile insurance be obtained.

We will have an interview with each applicant at Science Tokyo and provide a recommend to the Foundation of Corporate Friendship Network for Foreign Students.
9.6 Private Apartments and Shared Houses
(1) Guarantor
In Japan, a guarantor is required when signing a lease contract for an apartment or house. If you are not able to find anyone to be your guarantor, you can use one of the many private guarantee companies available. Please try to find a company that best suits your needs.
(2) Housing Support
Science Tokyo Housing Support can assist students or researchers searching for rooms. We provide information and news from rental property websites, companies, and real estate agencies.
For details

The Science Tokyo COOP offers a private apartment introduction service. If you rent an apartment introduced by COOP, a real estate agent fee is not required.
Science and engineering students
Science Tokyo COOP (Only in Japanese)
In addition, there are many shared houses in the Tokyo metropolitan area. In general, the contract procedure for shared houses is simpler than that for renting apartments.
9.7 Rules for Living in Japan
There are various rules and customs for living in dormitories or apartments in Japan. All international students are expected to follow the rules and observe good manners. At the bottom of the following web page, you can find tips for avoiding trouble and enjoying a fulfilling student life.
Independent Living in Tokyo
10．Commuter Passes and Student Discounts
Commuter passes, which may be good for a period of one, three, or six months, are a form of discounted travel. There are two kinds of commuter passes: student commuter passes and ordinary commuter passes. The cost of a student commuter pass is lower than that of an ordinary commuter pass.
10.1 Regular Students (degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students)
10.2 Non-Regular Students (Graduate Research Students, International Exchange Students, and International Visiting Students)
10.1 Regular Students (degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students)
Regular students (degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students) are eligible for a student commuter pass. You will be requested to show a Commuter Pass Purchase Certificate (Tsuugaku-teikiken-kounyu-shoumeisho) and your student ID card when purchasing the pass. Under Japanese law, Commuter Pass Purchase Certificates can only be issued for the least expensive route between the station nearest your home and the station nearest your campus. Hence, you will not be able to purchase a student commuter pass to travel to your part-time job or other destinations.
Commuter Pass Purchase Certificates are issued (the number of copies is limited) from automated certificate issuance machines at the Ookayama and Yokohama campuses. They are issued at the counter at Yushima Campus. Note that your student ID card is required, so you must collect it in person. You will need to keep the Certificate after using it to purchase a commuter pass, as it will be valid for the duration of your enrollment.
Regular students can also buy discounted student tickets. (Discounted student tickets are for journeys over 100 km one-way on JR lines, and cost 20 percent less than the regular fare. For details, please ask the staff at any JR station.) When purchasing a discounted student ticket, you will be requested to show a Student Discount Certificate (Gakuwarishou) and your student ID card. You can get the Student Discount Certificate from an automated certificate issuance machine.
10.2 Non-Regular Students (Graduate Research Students, International Exchange Students, and International Visiting Students)
Non-regular students are permitted to purchase a student commuter pass for Tokyu lines only.
Non-regular students cannot purchase discounted student tickets.

11.1 Procedures for Inviting Family Members to Japan on Short-Term Tourist Visas
If you would like to invite family to Japan on tourist visas, please contact the Japanese embassy or a travel agency in your home country for information on how to apply. For stays of 90 days or less, it is possible to apply for a “Temporary Visitor” visa. Depending on the status of the mutual visa exemption agreement between Japan and the country concerned, a visa may not be required for a short-term stay for tourism purposes.
11.2 Procedures for Inviting Your Family to Reside with You
If a foreign student wishes to invite family to reside with him/her in Japan, the student must obtain a Certificate of Eligibility beforehand. When applying for a Certificate of Eligibility, you are advised to contact the Regional Immigration Services Bureau in advance and prepare the necessary documents. You will always be required at the very least to submit your certificate of enrollment at Science Tokyo, your scholarship certificate, and a copy of the contract for your apartment.

Some company dormitories and public housing only provide single rooms. Moreover, some private apartments do not allow children. You should collect all the relevant information when looking for accommodation for you and your family.

Science Tokyo has four libraries: Ookayama Library, Ochanomizu Library, Konodai Library and Suzukakedai Library.
You need a student card to use the libraries. For those who do not own one despite being affiliated with Science Tokyo, we can issue a library card for you. Please bring a form of identification (hard copy) issued by Science Tokyo to the circulation counter.

13.2 Employment Support in Science and Engineering Departments
13.1 Student Career Support Services
The Student Success Support Room and Student Support Center provide career support
services by coordinating with faculty members in each Department. All services are open to
international students and some are available in English.
(1) Career Counseling
Science and engineering students
Career advisors will respond to all of your career-related queries in both English and Japanese.
Every week, each of our four career advisors spends a day on duty at the Ookayama Campus
and the Yokohama Campus.
- Example of Concerns Discussed in Career Counseling
・ Is it possible for international students to work in Japan?
・ What is a normal process for finding employment in Japan?
・ Do you have any tips for successful interviews?
・ What should I do to get a job in my field/in an unrelated field?
You can choose either face-to-face counseling or online counseling. You can schedule an
appointment from 30 days to 1 hour before the counseling session. However, counseling
sessions after 5 p.m. are reserved for appointments made on the same day. Additionally, for
same-day appointments, reservations will close by 4 p.m.
You can only book one appointment at a time.

Privately funded scholarships are divided into two types: one requires a recommendation from
a university, and the other requires no recommendation. The application process differs for the
two types. Detailed information about both kinds of scholarships is announced on the Science

Registration starts in September every year and you can register anytime during the year. For
