16. Science Tokyo Tsubame Scholarship for Doctoral Students
(Science and engineering students only)
Tokyo Tech, one of the parent institutions of Science Tokyo, established the Tsubame Doctoral
Student Scholarship in 2019 for doctoral students.
The Tsubame Scholarship for Doctoral Students aims to reduce the financial burden on
academically outstanding students so that they may concentrate on pursuing their doctoral studies.
The financial assistance is intended to prevent motivated students from missing out on the
opportunity to study at the Institute.
16.1 Eligibility
16.2 Scholarship Amount

16.1 Eligibility
Students who enrolled in a doctoral degree program (science and engineering fields) in or after April 2018 are eligible to apply.
Doctoral students are not eligible if any of the following is true:
1. They receive financial aid from programs that do not permit funding from other sources (e.g.,
recipients of the JSPS Research Fellowship for Young Scientists, MEXT Scholarship students,
recipients of overseas government scholarships, Science Tokyo Program for Development of
Next-Generation Front-Runners with Comprehensive Knowledge and Humanity (Science Tokyo
SPRING), Science Tokyo Program for Development of Co-creative Experts towards Top-level AI
Research (Science Tokyo BOOST)).
2. They receive income as working adults (e.g., regular employees of a company, individuals who
own a business).
3. They have exceeded the standard duration of their doctoral studies.

17.4 Traffic Rules in Japan
Lately, the number of the bicycle accidents has greatly increased. Please be aware of traffic
rules as accidents can have a devastating impact on the lives of those involved.
National police agency website “Traffic safety guidelines for pedestrians and cyclists”
Traffic Safety Rules
(1) Anti-theft registration
When riding a bicycle at night, you may be stopped by police who will ask to see your residence
card or other form of identification and check if you have a bicycle anti-theft registration sticker.
If the police find that the bicycle is registered in someone else’s name, you may be detained at
a police box for a long time, and possibly even charged with theft. To avoid this unpleasant
experience, take the following precautions:
・When purchasing a bicycle, be sure to register it at the store.
・If you receive a bicycle from a friend, fill out a “transfer of ownership” certificate together,
then take the document to a bicycle dealer to re-register the bicycle in your name.
・Never ride an abandoned bicycle.
(2) Automobile, motorcycle, and bicycle insurance
◆ Automobile and motorcycle insurance
If you plan to drive a car or ride a motorcycle, be sure to enroll in automobile or motorcycle insurance, since causing a traffic accident could make you liable to pay a large amount of compensation to any victims. Even if you only intend to drive or ride during a summer vacation trip or other short-term occasion, we strongly recommend that you buy insurance. Insurance policies can be purchased directly from an insurance company or through the University Co-op.
◆ Bicycle insurance
In many areas, including Tokyo and Kanagawa, it is mandatory to have insurance that covers liability if you injure someone in a bicycle accident. Insurance policies can be purchased directly from an insurance company or through the University Co-op.

Suzukakedai Campus renamed Yokohama Campus on April 1, 2026
April  1, 2026
Announcements
About Science Tokyo
Co-creating with society
Science Tokyo has changed the name of its Suzukakedai Campus to "Yokohama Campus," effective April 1, 2026.
Since its establishment in 1975, this campus has continued its educational and research activities for over half a century in northern Yokohama. Nestled in a lush green environment, it has produced numerous research achievements and progressed hand in hand with the local community.
The new campus name expresses Science Tokyo’s respect for the history of educational and research activities conducted in collaboration with the City of Yokohama, and the Institute’s determination to continue contributing to the development of the city.
The name "Suzukakedai" will continue to be used for certain facilities and events, such as Suzukakedai Library and Suzukake Science Day.
Having surpassed its 50th anniversary, Yokohama Campus is now taking a new step forward. While maintaining strong ties with the local community, it will fulfill its role as an important part of Science Tokyo as a University for International Research Excellence and return its achievements to society.

Tutors for international students
New international students arriving in Japan face various challenges and difficulties as they begin their new life, such as differences in language and lifestyle. Therefore, Science Tokyo has established a tutoring system for international students, where current students support new international students to smoothly settle in Japan and improve their academic and research outcomes. This system also aims to enhance the international understanding, cross-cultural awareness, and interest in international cooperation among the students serving as tutors.
What tutors shall do for new students
The support needed varies depending on the individual situation of each international student. To respond to the diverse needs of the students, tutors should proceed by confirming what kind of support is necessary for their assigned student. Here are some examples of support:
Examples of Support in Daily Life
Explaining Japanese culture and customs
Assisting with opening a bank account
Helping with procedures at city hall (residence registration, enrollment in National Health Insurance)
Assisting with shopping
Accompanying to hospitals
Examples of Academic Support
Introducing on-campus facilities (various offices, the library, classrooms, the Healthcare Center, etc.)
Providing support in laboratories
Assisting with course registration
Overview of the International Student Tutor System
Students hired by Science Tokyo as tutors provide support for the academic and daily lives of their assigned international students. For details on the hiring process, job duties, and reporting of working hours for tutors, please refer to the guidelines for your field below.

Airport arrival
Airport arrival
Arrival at the Airport
You will first arrive in Japan at one of the following airports: Fukuoka Airport (FUK), New Tokyo International Airport (NRT), Kansai International Airport (KIX), Central Japan International Airport (NGO), or Kumamoto Airport.
* If you arrive at New Tokyo International Airport (NRT), Kansai International Airport (KIX), or Central Japan International Airport (NGO), you should apply for transportation to Fukuoka Airport or Kumamoto Airport.
* If you arrive at Fukuoka Airport, we recommend you to take a highway bus from Fukuoka Airport or Hakata Bus Center to SAKURAMACHI Kumamoto Bus Terminal. This connection takes about two hours and costs approximately 2,500 yen. Before you leave Fukuoka, you should call your contact person at Kumamoto University and tell him/her your time of arrival at Kumamoto.
* If you arrive at Kumamoto Airport, you should take an airport limousine bus from Kumamoto Airport to SAKURAMACHI Kumamoto Bus Terminal. This connection takes about 50 minutes and costs 1000 yen.

Important Things to Do After Arriving in Kumamoto
Important Things to Do After Arriving in Kumamoto
Important Things to Do After Arriving in Kumamoto
Please read the "Handbook for International Students" carefully.
In addition, you should go through the following necessary procedures as soon as possible.
Your tutor or the staff at the International Student Office will help you to do them.
Notification (Change) of place of residence
Register for National Health Insurance
Register for National Pension System
Establish a bank account
Notification concerning the organization to which the foreigner belongs
In addition, those receiving Monbukagakusho (Japanese government, MEXT) scholarships should establish a postal saving account to receive scholarship.
1. Notification (Change) of Place of Residence
Foreigners who reside in Japan must go through notification (change) of place of residence within 14 days of finding a place to setlle down.
Please fill out the "Jyumin-Idoutodoke" form and submit it to the Kumamoto City Kuyakusho (Ward Office) along with your passport and residence card.
2. Registering for National Health Insurance
Foreign students who live in Japan longer than three months must register for National Health Insurance. Under the National Health Insurance plan, the Japanese government will cover 70% of your medical expenses if you get sick while in Japan. Please submit "Change in status/eligibility for National Health Insurance" and "Application for National Health Insurance" to Kumamoto City Kuyakusho (Ward Office). You need to notify when your address changed, brought your family to Japan or a baby is born. Please proceed to cancel your health insurance when you go back to your country.
3. Register for National Pension System
Not only Japanese citizens, but also foreign students over 20 years old must register for National Pension. You can complete the procedure for this at National Pension Section on Kumamoto City Kuyakusho (Ward Office) when you register for National Health Insurance. If your income is considered to be less than a pre-detemined income level, your insurance fee may be waived. Degree-seeking students (undergraduates and graduate school students) should apply for a "special exemption to student payment (Gakusei nofu tokurei)" and Non-degree seeking students (ex. special audit students, special research students) should apply for a "payment waiver (Menjo)".
4. Establishing a bank account
You can deposit money and transfer it to others. Both Higo Bank and Kumamoto Bank are located close to Kumamoto University.
In order to open up an account at a bank, you first need to fill out an account application form available at the bank. Please submit the form along with your passport and Certificate of Residence. It is usually necessary to have a name seal (called "inkan" in Japanese) when opening a bank account in Japan. For details, please visit
"Finance"
.
5. Notification concerning the organization to which the foreigner belongs
Students who belonged to another school in Japan such as university or language school before enrolling in Kumamoto University have to notify to the Ministry of Justice by visiting a Regional Immigration Office or sending a notification to the Tokyo Regional Immigration Bureau, within 14 days. You can notify on
the web
also.
*Attention Japanese Government Scholarship Students:
Please tell your postal savings account number to the international Affairs Division by designated date. Stipends for Japanese Government scholarship students are paid into postal savings accounts.
*Attention JASSO Scholarship Exchange Students:
Please tell your bank account number to the international Affairs Division by designated date.
Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
All international students at Kumamoto University have "College Student" visa status. You must apply for a permit to the Immigration Bureau through the International Student Office when you want to extend your stay, work part-time, bring your family to Japan, or re-enter Japan. In those cases, you should submit the forms for these permits to the International Student Office.

Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Certificate of Eligibility
International Students who will enroll in Kumamoto University need to apply for a Certificate of Eligibility. It takes about a month to issue it.
You must submit the following documents:
For privately funded students:
Application for Certificate of Eligibility (College Student)
One photo taken within 6 months (4 cm × 3 cm, with no hats on and no background scenery)
A copy of the Certificate of Admission
A financial statement (certficate of scholarship, certificate of bank balance, or a copy of bankbook)
A copy of passport
If you would like to bring your family members to Japan:
Application for Certificate of Eligibility (Dependent) (one for each family member)
One photo taken within 6 months (4 cm × 3 cm, with no hats on and no background scenery)
Postal stamps for the required amount.
Proof of Relationship
If you bring your husband or wife to Japan: Certificate of marriage
If you bring your children to Japan: Birth certificates for children
A copy of your Regidence Card (both sides)
Proof of ability to support your family members who are coming to Japan
In the case of Japanese government scholarship students: Certificate of Scholarship
In the case of privately funded students: Certificate of bank balances or copy of bank book
Certificate of Student Status
A copy of your and your dependants' passports

Tuition fee exemption
There is a tuition fee exemption system for students with financial difficulties. Full exemption and half exemption are available. These can be applied for the academic year following entrance to the university, but it is not guaranteed that the fees will be exempted. The application period every year is around February for the whole year and around July for the second semester. Please confirm the exact dates with the Student Life Division. Research students and non-regular students are not eligible to apply for tuition fee exemption.

Finance
Finance
Bank
You must submit the following items for opening a bank account:
1) Application form for opening a bank account
2)
Inkan
(Name Seal) or your signatureWhen opening an account, you usually need an inkan (your own name seal).International students don't necessarily need an inkan. Instead, your signature will suffice.
3) Passport
4) Certificate of Residence or Resident Card
The nearest banks from the university are Higo Bank, Kokai-bashi Branch.
- Higo bank, Kokai-bashi Branch
Office Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
(closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and national holidays)
Phone: (096) 343-2185
Post Office
You can send letters, packages, as well as make deposits and remit money at the post office. In regards to scholarships being received from the Japan Student Services Organization (a.k.a. JASSO) (which includes Japanese Government Scholarship Students, Japan-Korea Joint Government Scholarship Program to the students in Science and Engineer Departments Science and Engineering students, and Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students), JASSO pays scholarships directly into recipients' postal savings accounts. Therefore, please create a postal savings account if above-mentioned scholars have not done so already.
You must submit the following for opening a postal savings account:
1) Application form for creation a postal savings account
2) Inkan (Name Seal) or your signatureWhen opening an account, you usually need an inkan (your own name seal). International students don't necessarily need an inkan. Instead, your signature will suffice.
3) Passport
4) Certificate of Residence or Resident Card
The nearest post office from Kumamoto University is Kurokami-daini Post Office.
- Kurokami-daini Post Office
Office Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
(closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and national holidays)
Phone: (096) 343-2672

Getting to the International House
1.Kurokammi South Campus:
Administrative Office, Faculty of Science, Faculty of Engineering, Graduate School of Science and Technology, Center for Multimedia and Information Technologies, Center for Marine Environment Studies, Shock Wave and Condensed Matter Research Center
2.Kurokami North Campus
International Student Center
Student's Office, Health Care Center, Faculty of Letters, Faculty of Education, Faculty of Law, Research Center for University Education, University Library, University School for Disabled Children
3.Honjo and Kuhonji Campuses
Faculty of Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
Graduate School of Medical Sciences
School of Medicine
School of Health Sciences
Institute of Resource Development and Analysis
Center for AIDS Research
Institute of Molecular Embryogy and Genetics
4.Honjo Campus
University Hospital
5.Oe Campus
Faculty of Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences School of Pharmacy Graduate School of Pharmaceutical Sciences
6.International House Building C-E
7.International House Building A-B
From Kumamoto Station:
By Sanko-Bus: take a bus for Ozu (via Sanrigi and Jinnai) and get off at the "Ozeki-bashi Bus Stop."
By JR train: From Kumamoto Station, take the Hohi Line and get off at "Tatsudaguchi Station" and then walk to the International House on foot.
By Taxi: Approximately 15 minutes.
From Sakuramachi Bus Terminal:
By Sanko-Bus: Take a bus for Ozu or Musashigaoka and get off at the "Ozekibashi bus stop."
By Kumaden bus: Take a bus for Tatsudaguchi/Kusunoki-danchi and get off at the "Ozekibashi bus stop."
By Taxi: Approximately 15 minutes.
From Kumamoto Airport:
By Sanko Bus: Get on the Limousine Bus headed for the Sakuramachi Bus Terminal and get off at the terminal. Take a Kumamoto-Shiei Bus for Tatsudaguchi/Kurokami-danchi or the Sanko-Bus for Ozu/Musashigaoka. Get off at the "Ozekibashi bus stop."
By Taxi: Approximately 40 minutes.

Rental Fees and Charges
Due to the recent increase in maintenance costs and other expenses caused by inflation, we plan to raise the room fees for C, D and E and common service fees by 8% to 10% starting from April 2027.
We will notify residents via the International House website or email as soon as the decision is made.
The increased room fees and common service fees are expected to be the amounts listed in the table below.
1. Payment of rent, property usage charges, electricity and water expenses
(1) Residents of Building A and B
International Students
The invoices for rent, expenses for common service, electricity and water charges are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges at the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month. Couple and family rooms are equipped with a gas range. Residents need to initiate a contract. For details on how to apply, use and pay for gas, follow the instructions provided by the gas company and the International House office.
Researchers
The invoices for property usage charges, expenses for common service, electricity and water charges are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges at the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month. Since the rooms for researchers are equipped with a gas range, residents need to initiate a contract. For details on how to apply for, use and pay for gas, follow the instructions provided by the gas company and the International House office.
(2) Residents of Building C and D
International Students
The invoices for rent, expenses for common service, electricity and water charges are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges at the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month.
(3) Residents of Building E
International Students
The invoices for rent and expenses for common service are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges to the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month. Since electricity and water must be contracted by the residents directly with the utility companies, follow the instructions of the International Student Office and the International House office for these.
Non-smoking in University Campuses
From July 1, 2019,
Kumamoto University is
100% smoke-free campus
. This includes International House (inside and outside of the buildings). Thank you for your understanding and cooperation to prevent exposure to secondhand smoke.

title: 熊本大學：housing-guidelines-fall2026（116適用性待查）
text:
【第1頁】
別紙 ２                                                                       
To International Student s, 
                                  Director of Institute for Education and Student Affairs  
 
Kumamoto University International House  
(Dorm itory  for Internati onal Students)  Appl ication  
             
This is to notify international students that the International House for academic year  2026 (Fall  Semester)  is now open for 
application.  
1. Application Method  
Please apply through your academic supervisor who is eligible to  download the "Application Format" from the 
International Residence Management System  which is accessible from the campus only . International students before 
enrolling in Kumamoto University are not eligible to access to the System.  Your applicatio n will complete when the 
"Application Format" is registered on the International House Residence Management System.   
 
 URL：https://fgc.jimu.kumamoto -u.ac.jp/kokusai_kaikan/  
                       ※ We have moved to a new system since 2025.  
 
2. Register Deadline : 
 July  17, 20 26 
* Registration for new application should be done through your academic supervisor, so please send the completed 
Application Form to your academic supervisor as soon a s possible.  You will receive a n email f rom the system once it ’s 
successfully  submitted . If you do not receive the email , please  check  with your academic supervisor . 
* Applicant s, who wish to reside  in the International House  but have  not received the examination result yet,  should apply  
before  the result . However,  their residence permits of those who fail the examination will be cancelled . 
* Exchange students under agreements between  universities or faculties have  priority over  the other students . Please take 
note t here would not be enough rooms for all applicants in the case of a lot of applications.  
 Also, we may not be able to meet your preferred room type . The selection results will be announced  between late July to 
early August . 
 
3. Types of Room  
Type of Room  Building  Furnishings

4. Eligibility  (Applicants  must meet a ll of the following two  requirements ) 
  (1) New international students who will enroll in Kumamoto  Unive rsity  October 2026 . 
      *Exclusive of elective course students  (called kamokuto -rishusei  in Japanese)  
  (2) International students who have not lived at the International House before (exclu sive  of elective course students).  
 *International students who have lived  at the International House before, but re-enroll  in Kumamoto University  
after leaving Japan for a certain period are eligible to apply.  
 

【第2頁】
5. Period  of Residence   
Maximum 5 months or 11 months  
5 months: Late  September, 2026 ~ February  26, 202 7 
11 months : Late  September, 202 6 ~ August 2 7, 202 7 
*Due to the large number of students  moving out at the end of February and August, you may be asked to move out up to 
around two weeks earlier than the  permitted residence . 
*The above move -out deadlines of February and August are set to prepare  for new international students en roll ing in April 
and October of the following year, respectively. Please check with the academic affairs office of your respective department 
for the move -in start date  of late September . 
* Regular students can stay at the International House for half a year  only . 
* Applicants, who wish to have a specific period of residence, are advised to consult with  the International Students Office 
individually.   
If no consultation takes place , the application will be treated as either  of the above -mentioned residency periods.  
* Depending on the student's affiliation and status , a different period of stay may be set.  
 6. Fees  (JPY per month )  
Due to the recent increase in maintenance costs and other expenses caused by inflation, we plan to raise  
the room fee s for C, D and E and common  service fee s by 8% to 10% starting from  April 2027.  
We will notify residents via the International  House  website or email as soon as the decision is made.  
The increased room fees and common service  fees are expected to be the amoun ts listed in the table below.  
 
 
（1）A deposit will be charged separately when moving in . The deposit will be refunded after taking out the cleaning 
fee and key replacement fee , if any equipment and furniture have no damage.   
（2）Monthly rent is pro-rated on  a daily basis  when moving in or out in the middle of the month, but the common 
service charge  is fixed that  will not  be prorated  excluding September when residents need to move in based 
on Kumamoto University ’s instruction.    
  （3）All residents must rent Futon (Bedding) during each permitted residency period.  
This fee is  non-refundable even if you move out  before the end of your  permitted residency period .  
For details,  please refer to  the International House website.  
https://www.kumamoto -u.ac.jp/kokusaikouryuu/kokusaikouryuukaikan/ryoukin  
    （4）Utility fee is subject to change.

7. Responsibilities  
Residents  are required to obey the regulation s of the International House . If you feel  difficult to do so, you are advised to 
find any other accommodation other than International House . (We might force  residents to move out of Internat ional

The below regulations  are extracted from “Occupant Regulations ” which  will be provided to each resident upon moving in . 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
【Contact 】Person in charge /  KATSUNO, MASUDA  , International Student Office  
〒860-8555 2 -40-1 K urokami , Chuo Ward,  Kumamoto -city, K umamoto  
Phone: 096-342-2160 / Fax. 096 -342-2130 /  
E-mail: gji-ryugaku @jimu.kumamoto -u.ac.jp  
* Moving -in & out have to be taken during the office hours: between  9:00am  and 4:00pm  
(3:00pm for move -out) on weekdays. (Except for Saturday s, Sunday s, National holidays.)  
* Letting  guests stay overnight in  your room is strictly prohibited.   
*  The opposite gender is forbidden  to enter  the shared room except for renter’s family members.  
* You must not lend out or duplicate International House keys.  
* There may be occasions when staff need to enter  rooms without notice in order to do emergency 
checks on room equipment and furnishings.  
* Please dispos e of your garbage on the specified collection day at designated site.  
* Please  note that it is not possible to move in before the move -in date. If you wish to move in 
earlier, please make your own arrangements for hotels, etc.  
* Please park bicycles and motorcycles in designated parking places.  
* To keep the bed mattress clean, please rent futon(bedding).  
*  I-House is a smoke -free premises including  public spaces, shared areas or private rooms,  
   even outside of the buildings. We order you to move out if you smoke.  
* Do not keep or feed pets or other animals in the I -House.

Immigration and Pickup Service
Entry Procedures
Immigration inspection
Your passport and visa will be checked, and your status of residence and period of stay will be determined.
Baggage claim
After passing through immigration, pick up your baggage at the baggage claim area. If you cannot find your baggage, ask the staff there for assistance. Follow their instructions. Any late-arriving baggage will be sent to you as soon as possible. The flight charge for your baggage in this case will be covered by the airline.
Customs clearance
A customs officer will inspect your belongings. If you are carrying items such as alcoholic beverages or cigarettes, you may be required to pay a duty. Unaccompanied baggage that you had sent to Japan before your arrival must also be declared.
Pickup service (For Short-Term Exchange Students who are renting rooms at International House)
Kumamoto University staffs will pick you up at SAKURAMACHI Kumamoto Bus Terminal. The pickup service is available between 9:00 a.m. and about 4:00 p.m. on the designated date (except weekends and holidays).
Please complete a "Pickup Service Application Form" from a link sent by International Student Office before your departure. If you do not need the pickup service, please let us know your flight schedule.
If you require someone's help, please contact International Student Office (e-mail:
gji-ryugaku@jimu.kumamoto-u.ac.jp
Fax: +81-96-342-2103).

Money, Photos, Insurance
Money, Photos, Insurance
Money
Upon arrival in Japan, you will need some Japanese yen for transport and meals. Please exchange some money at the airport in advance of your arrival. If you are eligible for a JASSO scholarship, you will receive a relocation allowance and the first stipend of the scholarship about three weeks after your arrival. We strongly urge that you bring enough money to support yourself during this initial period (approx. $1,000 USD).
Photos
You will need photographs of yourself (about 7 pictures, sized 4.0 cm x 3.0 cm) for various formalities, such as completing your alien registration at City Hall and registering at Kumamoto University International House after your arrival.
Travel accident insurance
We recommend that you obtain travel insurance in case something happens to you or your luggage on your way to Japan.

Passports and Visas
Passports and Visas
All international students applying to study in Japan must have a student visa that will remain valid for the duration of their studies. Before arrival in Japan, you must meet several requirements, as explained below.
Passport
It may take a long time for you to receive a passport after you apply for it. We recommend that you apply for your passport from your home country as early as possible.
Visa
Make sure that you obtain the appropriate visa. You will receive a visa with a student status because your purpose for coming to Japan is to study. If you arrive in Japan with a different type of visa, you will have to go through complicated procedures to change your visa status to the ""college student" designation. To avoid this problem, please be sure to obtain a "college student" visa before traveling to Japan.
a. Exchange students and privately funded students
As soon as you receive your Acceptance Letter and Certificate of Eligibility from Kumamoto University, please apply for a visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate in your home country. You will need to submit the certificates, your passport, and some photos. The length of the application process depends on the country issuing the visa. Students who are eligible for JASSO scholarships will receive a Certificate of Scholarship. Please also submit this, if necessary, when you apply for a visa.
b. Japanese government scholarship students (University recommendation)
A "Letter of Approval" will be issued and sent to you. You may then contact your nearest Japanese embassy/consulate to apply for your visa to enter Japan.

Air Tickets
Air Tickets
Air Tickets
a. Exchange students and privately funded students
Please purchase the tickets for your flight on your own, and ensure that you will arrive in Japan by the designated date.
b. Japanese government scholarship students
(1) Booking …
A: Embassy Recommendation
Japanese embassy or travel agency will book an air ticket for you.
B: University Recommendation
Kumamoto University will book an air ticket for you.
Complete the application form and send it immediately to the international Student Office of Kumamoto University by e-mail.
*Write your contact address in your home country using the Roman alphabet (kanji characters can be included).
(2) Receipt
For an e-ticket (electronic ticket), you will receive an electronic ticket receipt or an electronic ticket passenger itinerary receipt (name varies by airline) via e-mail.
The boarding ticket is issued at the airline check-in counter on the departure date.
Note:
* You cannot change your flight schedule or cash in the air ticket supplied to you.
* Since the air ticket must be submitted to MEXT after it has been used, you must submit the boarding ticket stub to Kumamoto University upon arrival.
* Please note that you must pay the transportation fee from the Japanese international airport at which you first arrive to Kumamoto.

Travel Information
Travel Information
Flight schedule
Pickup Service is available for Short-Term Exchange Students who are renting rooms at International House. Please complete a "Pickup Service Application Form"
from a link sent by International Student Office before your departure. If we cannot meet you as scheduled, you have to go to International House by yourself. If you are unable to depart as scheduled for some reasons, please contact us immediately (Tel: +81-96-342-2103 E-mail:
gji-ryugaku@jimu.kumamoto-u.ac.jp
).
Baggages
Generally, you are allowed to bring a maximum of 20 kg of baggage with you free of charge on the plane. If you exceed this limit, you will have to pay excess weight charges. You should bring only the most necessary items when you come to Japan. Once you settle in, you can buy most things you need in Japan, or you can have items sent to you from your home country. If you want to send unaccompanied baggage to Japan ahead of your arrival, please check with us first. Do not send it to the airport or university without consulting with us in advance.
Customs regulations
Your possessions, even those for personal use during your stay in Japan, will be inspected at customs and may be subject to customs duty. Please fully check the customs regulations before traveling to Japan.
In Japan, possession of any of the following is prohibited by law:
a. Stimulants, marijuana, and any other illegal drugs
b. Firearms and swords
c. Pornography (books/videotapes)
d. Articles that infringe upon such things as trademark rights and patent rights, e.g., counterfeit goods, etc.)
e. Wild animals and plants, or related goods that are regulated by the Washington Treaty.
(Do not violate this law, or you will be strictly punished and your scholarship will be revoked.)
If you bring animals and plants (including seeds and fruits) into Japan, you must go through quarantine. As there are many prohibited/restricted items, please carefully check the belongings you intend to bring into Japan; otherwise, your items may be confiscated.

Short-Term Exchange Program
"
Short-Term Exchange Program
(Brochure)"
Purpose
Kumamoto University Short-Term Exchange Program is designed for full-time foreign undergraduate students in their 2nd year or above from universities that have a student exchange agreement with Kumamoto University. The program offers courses on Japanese language, Japanese and Asian society and culture, advanced science and technology. At Kumamoto University, there are both half- and full-year programs, and students retain full-time student status at their home universities. This program encourages promotion of cultural and academic interactions between Kumamoto University and partner university students.
Available Courses and Qualifications
E Course (Program in English)
Students in this course mainly take Short-Term Exchange Program classes taught in English and some Japanese classes. Additionally, they have opportunities to attend non-credit Japanese language course for beginners during their stay.  Students who wish to take other classes must have a  consulatation with the office staff in advance. Also, those other classes will not be calculated towards program completion.
Eligibility
E Course
seeking applicants should be 2
nd
year students or above at the time of program start.
For non-native English speakers, submission of a copy of TOEFL score (iBT 61 or higher) is required (IELTS score is also accepted).
*Chinese CET, Indonesian ELPT are NOT adequate.
*A letter from a professor
CANNOT be accepted
as a proof of language proficiency.
Applicants should be physically and mentally capable of completing their studies for designated periods.
*Applicants should be able to hold the student VISA when she/he arrives in Japan.
J Course (Program in Japanese)
Students in this course mainly take classes in specialized subjects for undergraduate students of each faculty, as well as classes of the Japanese language. Also, they can take general education classes and Short-Term Exchange Program classes taught in English.
Eligibility
J Course
Applicants should be non-Japanese students.
Applicants for
J Course
should be 2
nd
year students or above at the time of program start.
Applicants should have Japanese ability equivalent to JLPT N2 level or better.
*A letter from a professor
CANNOT be accepted
as a proof of language proficiency.
Applicants should be physically and mentally capable of completing their studies for designated periods.
*Applicants should be able to hold the student VISA when she/he arrives in Japan.
Period of Acceptance
Students are accepted for a half year or one full year that starts in either October or April.
Application Package
Please contact the person in charge of outbound program at your university for application documents. Kumamoto University does not accept any mails sent by indivitual students.

Rules for living in the International House and Apartments
Garbage disposal
・Observe designated times, days and places for putting out garbage.
・Put out your garbage on the morning of the designated day.
・Follow the garbage sorting rules.
Washing machines
・Be particularly careful about noise and water leaks. Avoid doing your laundry early in the morning or late at night.
・ Make sure the drainage hose does not get knocked out of the drainpipe. If you do not connect properly, it may cause water leakage and cause troubles in the rooms on the lower floors.
Fire Hazards
・Make sure you extinguish cigarettes.
・Do not smoke whtin the site.
・Be careful not to leave electrical appliances on (iron, heating appliances, etc.).
Miscellaneous
・Make sure you read and understand your rental contract and follow the conditions.
・Do not have guests to stay or sublet the apartment, even for short peiods, without the landlord's permission.
・Do not leave personal belongings on the communal corridors and passageways.
・Keep your apartment clean.

熊本大学における授業料の改定について
熊本大学における授業料の改定について
熊本大学は、将来にわたって質の高い教育・研究環境を維持・向上させ、地域および国際社会に貢献し続けるため、令和9年度（2027年度）より授業料の改定を行うことを決定いたしました。
学長メッセージ
授業料改定にあたっての背景と決意
熊本大学は、昨今の急速な社会情勢の変化に対応するため、新たな学環・課程の設置や、教育研究活動の機能強化に対する積極的な投資を行ってまいりました。その結果、研究大学として「地域中核・特色ある研究大学強化促進事業」（J-PEAKS）に採択されるなど、多額の研究費を獲得し、地域への貢献についても全国的に高い評価をいただいております。
また、本学では自らの努力として、土地の有効活用やネーミングライツの導入による自己財源の確保、業務効率化による経費の節減、さらには、私が陣頭指揮を執った「物価高騰緊急支援寄附募集キャンペーン」など、財務改革に全力で取り組んでまいりました。
しかしながら、昨今の物価高騰や賃上げなどの影響は、こうした自助努力による節減効果を上回っております。そのため、本来であれば将来の学生のために確保しておくべき資源まで取り崩し、大学運営に対応している現状で、状況は極めて厳しいものとなっています。
こうした状況に対し、本学では様々な会議等で議論を重ねるとともに、黒髪南・黒髪北・本荘の各キャンパスにおいて対面とオンラインを併用した意見交換会や、留学生を対象とした意見交換会を計１０回開催いたしました。これらを通じ、学生や保護者の皆様をはじめとする多くの方々と直接対話する場を設け、大変貴重なご意見をいただきました。
そして、最終的に「大学が前向きに発展を続け、質の高い教育・研究・サービスを継続するためには、授業料の改定は避けて通れない苦渋の選択である」という結論に至りました。
今回の改定により確保した財源は、これまで先送りになっていた老朽化した施設の修繕や、全学的な無線LAN環境の充実、ソフトウェア（Microsoft 365）の無償提供など、学生の皆様が直接恩恵を実感できる教育環境の整備に確実に充当してまいります。
また、経済的に困難な状況にある学生への支援につきましても、学びの機会を保障するための措置を徹底して講じてまいります。
皆様のご理解とご協力を賜りますよう、心よりお願い申し上げます。
熊本大学長　小川　久雄

Revision of Tuition Fees at Kumamoto University
Kumamoto University has decided to revise its tuition fees from the 2027 academic year in order to maintain and further enhance a high-quality education and research environment over the long term, and to continue contributing to the local community and international society.
Message from the President
Background to the Tuition Fee Revision and Our Commitment
In response to rapidly changing social and economic conditions in recent years, Kumamoto University has been actively investing in the establishment of new interdisciplinary schools and degree programs, as well as in the strengthening of its education and research functions. As a result, the University has been selected for the Program for Forming Japan’s Peak Research Universities (J-PEAKS), has secured substantial research funding, and has been highly recognized nationwide for its contributions to the region.
At the same time, the University has made every effort to reform its finances through its own initiatives. These include securing independent sources of revenue through the effective use of University-owned land and the introduction of naming rights, reducing expenditures through operational efficiency, and carrying out the Emergency Fundraising Campaign in Response to Rising Prices, which I personally led.
However, the financial impact of rising prices and wage increases has exceeded the savings achieved through these efforts. As a result, the University is currently being forced to draw on resources that should have been preserved for future students in order to sustain its operations. The financial situation has therefore become extremely severe.
In response to this situation, the University held extensive discussions regarding the tuition fee revision through a series of meetings. It also organized a total of ten in-person and online dialogue sessions at the Kurokami South, Kurokami North, and Honjo campuses, including sessions specifically for international students. Through these opportunities, we engaged in direct dialogue with students, parents and guardians, and many other members of the University community, and received a great deal of valuable feedback.
After careful consideration, we ultimately reached the conclusion that revising tuition fees is a difficult but unavoidable decision if the University is to continue developing in a positive direction and maintaining high-quality education, research, and services.
The additional revenue generated by this revision will be dedicated to improving the educational environment in ways that will directly benefit students. This includes repairing aging facilities that have long required attention, improving the campus-wide wireless LAN environment, and providing Microsoft 365 services free of charge to students.
We will also take comprehensive measures to support students facing financial difficulties and ensure that they are able to continue their studies.
I sincerely ask for your understanding and cooperation.
Hisao Ogawa
President, Kumamoto University

】
Effective Date and Scope of the Revision
Effective Date:
The revised tuition fees will take effect from the 2027 academic year.
Scope:
The revision will apply to students enrolled in undergraduate schools/faculties, interdisciplinary schools, graduate schools/faculties, the Diploma Course in Special Education, and the Yogo Teacher Training Special Course, as well as research students, credited auditors (excluding students enrolled through the High School-University Articulation Program), special auditing students, and special research students.
*
The revised tuition fees will apply simultaneously to students in all year levels.

* Application fees and admission fees will not be changed as a result of this revision.
* From the 2028 academic year onward, the University will introduce the concept of a sliding adjustment system, under which tuition fees will be reviewed periodically in light of price trends.
Expansion of Financial Support Measures
In conjunction with the tuition fee revision, the University will provide the following support to students who may face difficulty continuing their studies for financial reasons.
For households eligible for tuition reductions of two-thirds or one-third under the National Higher Education Study Support System, the amount of the tuition increase will be waived.
Under Kumamoto University’s own support system, the household income threshold for eligibility under the National Higher Education Study Support System will be raised from 3.8 million yen to 4.25 million yen, in consideration of rising prices. For households newly covered by this expansion, the amount of the tuition increase will be waived. The same support will also be provided to graduate students and other eligible students under the University’s own support system.
Use of the Additional Revenue (Plan for Improving the Educational Environment)
The additional revenue generated by the tuition fee revision will be used as a priority for the following purposes.
Restoration of education and research expenses:
Securing funds for equipment purchases and facility repairs that had been reduced due to rising prices.
Enhancement of the IT environment:
Upgrading and improving the campus wireless LAN infrastructure, and providing Microsoft 365 services free of charge to students.
Improvement of the quality of education:
Assigning additional instructors to expand course offerings, and enhancing student support systems.
In addition, the University plans to renovate the Faculty of Letters and Law South Building and the Student Hall, and to repair restrooms and air-conditioning systems.
The University will also use the results of future student surveys to further improve support based on students' needs.

短期留学プログラム
目的
熊本大学短期留学制度は、大学間学生交流協定大学の正規課程に在籍する外国籍の学部2年次以上を対象とした制度で、日本語習得、日本及びアジアの社会文化、先端の科学技術、諸外国の学生との交流等に関心を持つ学部レベルの外国人学生に、母校に在籍のまま最長1年間の短期留学の機会を提供しています。また、諸外国の学生や熊本大学の学生との交流を育むことを目的としています。
プログラム
Eコース（英語によるプログラム）
主に、英語による短期留学プログラム科目を受講します。また、日本語科目も受講できます。所属学部開講専門科目や教養教育科目も受講できますが、修了要件には含まれません（注：専門科目及び教養教育科目は基本的に日本語で行われます）。
Jコース（日本語によるプログラム）
主に、各学部開講専門科目及び日本語科目を受講します。また、教養教育科目及び英語による短期留学プログラム科目も受講できます。

To receive a student visa from the Japanese Embassy or Consulate, you need a Certificate of Eligibility (COE). 
The Ryukoku University Center for the Promotion of Global Education  (R-Globe) Office will apply for this 
(in Japan) on your behalf, after we receive all your required application documents. It generally takes six to 
eight weeks for the Certificate to be issued, so be sure to submit all your materials as soon as possible to avoid 
any possible delay. Once we receive the Certificate of Eligibility , we will send it together with the Letter of 
Acceptance to you in a “ Welcome Package”, addressed to your home university . Once you receive th ese 
documents, please take the Certificate of Eligibility and the Letter of Acceptance to the Japanese Embassy in 
your own country to apply for your student visa.   
 
 
 
 
◎Regarding the ID photograph, please assure that the photo fits  these specifications: facing front, showing 
the upper half of the body (shoulders and above), with no objects or shadows in the background. 
◎Please select the Faculty/Graduate School that is most closely related to your home university major.  
◎Please note that you need to have obtained a Bachelor ’s degree and currently belong to a Graduate School 
at your Home University before arrival if you intend to enroll in any of the Graduate Schools of Ryukoku 
University.

to submit of the “Grid for Self-Assessment of Japanese Language Skills” as a means for us to evaluate your 
Japanese language skills. Please first read the “Explanation for Self-Assessment of Japanese Language Skills” 
and then fill out the “Grid for Self-Assessment of Japanese Language Skills” as instructed.

There are five patterns of study available to Exchange Students.  
 
 
 
 
This study course is designed for students with no Japanese language study experience (or for those who have 
only studied Japanese for a minimal amount of time) and for students who will not come to Japan with the 
goal of focusing on Japanese language studies. All classes are offered in English.

①  JEP-E (Japanese Experience Program in Kyoto – In ENGLISH) 

【第5頁】
4 
 
Exchange Students take classes in  Japanese Society and Culture (Japanese History, Society, Economics, 
Business Administration, Law, Technology, Literature and Movies, Media and Arts, Pop Culture, etc.. Students 
also learn about Kyoto ’s rich culture and traditions, including Buddhist Thought. An introductory language 
class, taking place three times a week, serves as a first exploratory step into the world of Japanese.  
 
For this study course, we strongly recommend that students whose native language is not English  have 
previously achieved an English test score equivalent to TOEFL PBT 500. 
 
Students are also eligible to register for a selection of English-taught classes in our regular Faculties/Graduate 
Schools. 
 
If the J EP-E  study course is selected on the application form, this decision may not be changed once your 
application form has been submitted. Furthermore, students who have a one-year exchange term and initially 
register for this study course will continue taking JEP-E courses in their second semester. 
 
 
 
 
This study course offers classes taught mostly in Japanese. It is composed of ① Japanese language classes 
and ② elective subjects (mostly taught in Japanese) focusing on various aspects of Japanese culture and 
society.  
 
Japanese classes are offered from the upper beginner to advanced levels, divided according to the Common 
European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) “ Can-Do” goals. Focusing on practical use of the 
language, students participate in field trips and give presentations.  Elective classes make the most of the 
university’s location in Kyoto, the heart of Japanese traditions and culture. Classes in Japanese Culture, History, 
Literature, Society, Religion, Economics, Business Administration, Education, Law, Science, and Pop Culture 
are offered. (In addition to electives taught in Japanese, we also offer a selection of electives taught in English.)  
 
Students are also eligible to register for a selection of English-taught classes in our regular Faculties/Graduate 
Schools. 
 
We recommend that students in this course have previously studied the Japanese language for at least 300 
hours, or that they have previously achieved a level of N4 on the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JCLP). 
Furthermore, with regards to all JEP-J Applicants: if it is determined by our Japanese Placement Test that you 
do not meet the necessary Japanese level, you will be required to join the JEP-E study course. 
 
 
 
 
 
Participants in the [JEP-J] study course  who place in Class 4 or above  on the Japanese Placement Test 
administered during Orientation Week are eligible to enroll in classes within our regular Faculties or Graduate 
Schools, in addition to subjects from the JEP-J curriculum. Students placed in Class 4 or above have freedom 
in the degree they wish to participate in the JEP-J study course. It is also possible to arrange one’s schedule in 
such a way that there is a focus on selected Faculty/Graduate School subjects of interest.

Ryukoku has three campuses in and around Kyoto. These campuses are close to train lines and within easy 
reach of each other, so you should be able to commute easily between them.  
*There are free shuttle buses between the campuses throughout the day, w ith Fukakusa as the central campus. 
(From Fukakusa to Omiya: 20 Minutes; From Fukakusa to Seta: 40 minutes).  
 
 
 
 
◆FUKAKUSA 
FUKAKUSA Campus, located in southern Kyoto, is the main campus.  
The Center for the Promotion of Global Education and all the JEP Kyoto 
classes are located on this campus. The Faculties of International Studies, 
Economics, Business Adminis tration and Law, Policy Science, along 
with 1st and 2nd Year subjects of the Faculty of Letters and the Faculty of 
Psychology, and the Junior College are located here.  
 
◆OMIYA 
OMIYA Campus is our original campus (founded in 1639), and is located 
in central Kyoto, just beside historic Nishi Hongwanji Temple.  3rd and 
4th Year subjects of the Faculty of Letters and the Faculty of Psychology 
are taught here, and the campus provides an ideal calm and relaxed 
atmosphere for study and research. 
 ◆SETA 
SETA Campus, located in Shiga Prefecture’s “Biwako Culture Park”, is 
surrounded by nature and is the newest and largest campus, The Faculties 
of Advanced Science and Technology, Sociology and Agriculture are 
located here.

IMPORTANT: Common Financial Problems After Arrival 
 
It is always the case at the beginning of the semester that a few students have a very difficult time because they 
are not able to use the bank cards which they have brought with them from abroad, and therefore are not able 
to withdraw the necessary funds for their everyday lives.  
 
① Please be sure to confirm with your card company/bank that: (1) you will immediately be able to withdraw 
funds after arriving in Japan with your card, and (2) that you know exactly how to use the card. Please 
make it a point to remember your pin number to avoid having your account blocked. 
② It is sometimes the case that students do not inform the bank in their home country of their exchange study 
period, and their bank card is frozen due to sudden use in another country. Please be sure to inform your 
bank that you will be studying abroad to avoid this problem.  
③ There is often a daily limit for withdrawing money internationally from one’s bank in their home country. 
Please be well aware of what the daily limit is, so you can surely make initial dormitory payments, as well 
as have enough for initial living expenses. If your bank will not allow you to withdraw enough  money 
shortly after your arrival, please be sure to bring sufficient funds with you. 
 
 
 
 
Under the Japanese Immigration Laws, it is compulsory for all Exchange Students who will be in Japan for at 
least three months to enter the Japanese National Health Insurance system, even if one has insurance in their 
home country. The insurance fees are estimated to cost 1500yen to 2000yen per month. Enrolment in Japanese 
National Health Insurance can be carried out at the Ward Office closest to your Japanese residence. If you feel 
it is necessary, you might also like to purchase international health insurance in your home country before 
leaving for  Japan. More information on Japanese National Health Insurance will be provided during 
Orientation Week.

behavior . Please respect the privacy of others and behave appropriately so all residents 
can have an enjoyable university life. 
Ryukoku University International Student Dormitories 
General Rules 


【第13頁】
12 
 
 
 
 
 
① Please inform NASIC【※】 of your check-in date at least 2 weeks in advance. 
【※】[NASIC is the private company which manages the dormitories on be half of the Center for the 
Promotion of Global Education (R-Globe) Office]. 
 
② Please sign the [Pledge] and return it to NASIC. 
 
③ If you do not have a Japanese bank account when entering the dormitory, an account will be  
established for you at Yucho Ginko (Japan Post Bank). 
Please fill in the form to open an account and submit it to your Dormitory Tutor by the designated date.  
<Necessary Materials> 
■Application for Opening an Account 
■Residence Card Copy (issued upon your arrival in Japan) 
 
④ Regarding your First Payment 
For those s taying at [Mitra-kan], [Ryukoku International House], and [Ryukoku Kaikan]: 
Please make your payment of the Security Deposit and <First Time> Usage Fees [Rent, Utilities, Bedding 
(optional)] at the nearest convenience store shortly after your arrival. This payment must be made in cash. IT 
IS NOT POSSIBLE TO PAY BY CREDI T OR DEBIT CARD. Also, please note t hat Yucho Ginko 
(Japan Post Bank) does not offer online banking services. 
 
⑤ Security Deposit  
In principle, t he  security deposit will be returned when you check- out of the dormitory. However, if you 
have failed to pay your room rent or utilities fees, or if payment is required for any damages caused to the 
room or dormitory, the required fees will be deducted from this security deposit. If the amount required 
exceeds the amount of the security deposit, a bill will be sent to you for the excess amount. Students with a 
room rental waiver are not required to pay a security deposit. 
 
⑥ Automatic Account Withdrawal 
Room rent and utilities fees will be automatically withdrawn from your bank account on a designated day 
of the month. Please be sure to register your bank account as soon as it has been established! 
 
For those s taying at [Mitra-kan], [Ryukoku International House], and [Ryukoku Kaikan]: 
Each month’s room rent and utilities expenses will be automatically withdrawn from your bank account on 
the 6th of each month (in the case that the 6 th is a weekend or national holiday, on the following business 
day). 
※A utomatic withdrawal is possible from any Japanese bank. However, those who have not formerly  
opened a Japanese bank account will have an account establ ished at Y ucho Ginko (Japan Post Bank ) 
after their arrival in Japan. Please be sure to fill in this account on your automatic withdrawal form. 
 
⑦ Move-In Day 
  You will be given guidance by either a Resident Supporter【※】or the Dormitory Manager. 
  【※】The Resident Supporters are Japanese students of Ryukoku University who live in the dormitories 
to provide international students with assistance regarding their daily lives at the dorms and at the 
university in general. If you have any difficulties, please either consult either the Resident Supporters or 
the Center for the Promotion of Global Education (R-Globe) Office. 
  
Admission Procedures 

【第14頁】
13 
 
 
 
 
 
All dormitory residents (including students with a room rental waiver) are required to pay monthly utilities 
fees, even during break periods in between semesters. 
 
If a room is occupied for less than 15 days of any calendar month, rent will be calculated by the day. If the 
room is occupied from the 15th of the month on, the cost of one month will be charged. 
 
If a [SINGLE] room at Ryukoku International House is o ccupied for the first eight days of the month, he/she 
will be charged according to the following: 
 
(Int
ernational Student: 1 month rent 35,000JPY <Room Rent: 25,000JPY , Utilities 10,000JPY> 
↓ 
(35,000 JPY ÷ 30 days ×8 days = 9,333.3333 JPY  [Final charge: 9,333 JPY] ） 
Calculation Method: Monthly Fee ÷30 (days) × Number of Days Occupied. All decimal points are cut. 
 
 
 
 
 
①Due to the great number of students arriving in March and August, Occupants checking out must depart by 
March 20 or August 20 (If this  day falls on a weekend or public holiday, checkout must take place on the 
previous day). Rent and utilities fees will be calculated according to [Rules: Dorm Rent and Utilities] above. 
 
② Rental fees, once paid, will not be refunded except in special circumstances.  Not ification of leaving the 
dormitory must be submitted at least one month in advance. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
① Please be sure to submit a “Leaving the Dormitory ” form to your Resident Supporter by the 7 th of the 
month previous to the month you plan to depart. If you fail to turn in the form by that time, even if you 
plan to reside in your room for only 14 days or less in the following month, you will be charged the full 
rent amount. 
② Clean your room and remove your belongings before checking out. 
 
③ One Week before Checkout: Your Resident Supporter will conduct a room check. 
 
④  On Checkout Day : Your Resident Supporter will conduct a room check. This room check is required! 
⑤ Once your electricity fee has been calculated and the condition of your room checked, your Security 
Deposit will be refunded. 
■In the following cases, occupants will be required to leave the Dormitory: 
◎ Termination of studies at Ryukoku University 
◎ Expiration of contract 
◎ Rejection of application to extend one’s Period of S tay 
◎ Decision by the university that the occupant is no longer eligible to continue living in the dormitory 
Rules: Dorm Rent and Utilities 
Rules Regarding Incoming/Outgoing 
 
Checking Out Procedures 

【第15頁】
14 
 
◎ Where delayed payment or compensation exceeds the rental deposit amount 
◎ Failure to obey dormitory rules 
◎ Deliberate disobedience of university guidelines and instructions 
◎ Non-payment of rental fees and bills 
◎ Failure to fulfill one’s obligations as a dormitory resident 
 
■Leaving the Dormitory During the Residence Ter m 
If you wish to leave the dormitory before the resident period expires, notification must be provided to NASIC 
*AT LEAST* one month in advance. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
※土日に退寮することは避けてください。 
 
 
Please observe the regulations: 
①Dormitory property is not to be altered or misused in any way. 
②No economic or political activity may be carried out within the dormitory. 
③Dormitory furnishings or equipment are not to be removed. 
④Potential fire hazards such as gas ranges are not to be used outside designated areas 
⑤Occupants should follow dormitory rules and respect Japanese customs. 
⑥Do not disturb fellow residents or people living in the surrounding neighborhood. 
（e.g. making loud noise, leaving rubbish in the corridor/on the streets etc.） 
⑦Care should be taken to keep both one’s room and the communal living areas clean and sanitary. 
⑧Fires, thefts, etc. should be reported immediately 
 
●Cohabitation is prohibited. 
A single room may only have 1 occupant. 
 
●Entrance to other Res idents’ rooms is prohibited. 
You may not enter the rooms of other Residents, even in the case of friends. 
 
●Overnight guests are not permitted. 
Family and friends are not allowed to stay overnight in the dormitory. They are required to leave the 
dormitory premises by the curfew designated by each dormitory. 
 
●Smoking 
Smoking is not allowed within dormitory premises belonging to Ryukoku University (even outside the 
building) 
 
●Overnight Trips 
If you go away for an extended period or return to your home country, you must contact the Center for 
the Promotion of Global Education Office at least 1 week in advance. Fill out a Contact Addre ss Form 
and turn it in to the Dormitory Manager. 
 
  
Mandatory Code of Conduct 
Please note that it is not possible to check out of the 
dormitory on a Saturday or Sunday. 

【第16頁】
15 
 
●Use of Parking Facilities 
Please put an identification sticker on your bicycle (These stickers can be attained from t he Resident 
Supporters). Do not leave your bicycle at the dormitory  after you move out. In the case of theft, please 
report it directly to the police (not the University). 
Ryukoku University will not be held responsible for any cases of theft. 
 
●P ets  
Pets are strictly forbidden in the dormitory.  
 
●M ailbox  
Affix your name to your dormitory mailbox and be sure to check it at least once a day. 
 
 
 
 In addition to the rules above, each dormitory has its 
own regulations. If you fail to follow the regulations, 
you will be asked to leave the dormitory.

title: 龍谷大學：cefr-reference（116適用性待查）
text:
【第1頁】
Explanation for Self-Assessment of Japanese Language Skills 
 
 
Ryukoku University launches the Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP) for international exchange students 
in the 2026 Academic Year.  
 
The goal of this program is to take advantage of the benefits of living in Japan in order to ① Gain a variety of 
experiences both within and outside of Ryukoku University and ② Improve one’s Japanese language skills 
and gain insights into the societies and cultures of various countries through interactions with Japanese students 
and other international students.  
 
To achieve this, the program incorporates project -based learning in Japanese classes, such as through 
interviews and surveys. It also makes use of Japan’s social and cultural settings – especially the unique location 
of Kyoto – by including activities such as the observation of festivals and other traditional events. 
 
 
< Class Example (JSP-B Class) > 
Topic Objectives Activities 
Travel and 
Transportation 
When presenting about one’s country and 
hometown, if there is adequate preparation 
ahead of time, can provide a somewhat 
detailed introduction about famous places, 
famous items, etc. 
・Learn vocabulary and expressions to explain  
one’s hometown and to explain both one’s 
town and the places one has been 
・Make a poster to introduce one’s hometown 
Emergency 
Situations 
In the case of an accident or disaster, can  
understand an explanation or instructions if 
the speaker’s accent is sharp. 
・Read an evacuation drill notice for information.  
Know important details at the time of evacuation 
・Visit the Kyoto City Disaster Prevention  
Center and listen to the explanation and 
instructions 
 
Student Life Understands how school circumstances 
differ according to country and region and 
is able to express (to some extent) one’s 
own opinions in detail. 
・Through texts, gain an understanding of  
education in Japan 
・Read a pamphlet of Ryukoku University- 
affiliated Heian Junior/Senior High School and 
understand the contents 
・Visit Ryukoku University-affiliated Heian  
Junior/Senior High School to observe a class 
and have a discussion with the instructors 
・Give a presentation on one’s findings from the  
visit 
 
Different 
Cultures 
With enough prior preparation, can provide 
a somewhat detailed speech about the 
differences between Japan and one’s home 
country, as well as Japan’s surprising 
aspects. 
・Attend the Gion Festival and watch the  
procession of Yamahoko floats 
・Conduct an interview in the Fushimi  
Momoyama shopping arcade 
・Provide a five-minute speech on the theme of  
cultural differences 
 
 
 
 

【第2頁】
 
Furthermore, with the aim of broadening students’ practical Japanese language skills, objectives are set and 
class activities are carried out by using the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) “Can Do” 
system as a reference. Using this standardized  system, the students’ home university Japanese language 
instructors and other related individuals can share Japanese language learning progress information more easily. 
In addition, our curriculum is composed of designated classes which align with the  CEFR levels. Students in 
higher-level classes are eligible to enroll in regular undergraduate or graduate-level subjects. 
 
< Organization of Classes > 
 
Japanese Classes in the Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP) are organized into four levels (JSP-Ⅱ ~ JSP-Ⅴ) 
which adhere to the CEFR framework. For each skill (Listening, Reading, Interaction, Speaking, Writing), 
learning objectives are set using “Can-Do” statements. The table below shows provides an overview of the 
“Can-Do” objectives for each class. 
 
Can-Do Objective Examples (by Class) 
Class Target 
Level 
Can-Do Objectives 
JSP-Ⅴ 
B2.2 
The student Is able to use the language fluently, accurately, and effectively on a 
wide range of subjects. Communication is natural, using correct grammar and a 
level of politeness appropriate for the situation. Interviews are carried out 
smoothly and effectively, with questions adjusted to fit the other party and an 
ability to draw out topics of great interest to the interviewee. The student is then 
able to write an article by summarizing the contents, selecting important points 
and including supplemental facts. The student absorbs numerous points of view 
in order to gain a broader understanding of Japanese culture, one’s own culture, 
and the home culture of other international students. 
B2.1 
The student is able to converse fluently and naturally, emphasizing points which 
are important to oneself and explaining related points in detail. The student is 
assertive in firmly explaining the basis of his/her own perspective. Regarding 
his/her field of interest, is able to integrate many pieces of information from 
their source and present them as grounds for an argument. In an interview, asks 
questions relevant to the other party and can draw out various topics of interest. 
Can gather the main points and compose an article with the reader in mind. 
Absorbs numerous points of view in order to gain a broader understanding of 
Japanese culture, one’s own culture, and the home culture of other students. 
 
B1.2 
When conducting a questionnaire, the student puts together results and is able to 
provide a simple presentation using graphs and data. Can put together a short 
article and speech and can state one’s opinion. Is also able to answer detailed 
questions.  Can find the information needed from a variety of informational 
sites, etc.. Is able to conduct an easy interview while confirming information 
and asking related questions, and can combine the results and compose an 
article. 
 
 
 
 

【第3頁】
JSP-Ⅳ B1.1 
With preparation, is able to give a detailed presentation. Can converse concretely 
on topics of interest. Is able to read and understand short and easy sentences. 
Can write short sentences about familiar content and topics of interest. Is able to 
understand and respect both similarities and differences between one’s own 
culture, that of Japan, and that of other countries. 
JSP-Ⅲ A2.2 
Can understand regularly used sentences and expressions regarding topics 
directly related to oneself such as personal information, family information, 
shopping, one’s neighborhood and work, etc. Can exchange information about 
short and regular, everyday matters. Can explain, in easy words, necessary 
information about one’s background and daily circumstances. 
JSP-Ⅱ A2.1 
On short and familiar topics, can attain limited information by reading and 
listening. Can make a simple presentation and write a report with short 
sentences. Can converse and answer questions on simple, everyday topics. 
 
Class placement is determined comprehensively based on the results of the “Self -Assessment of Japanese 
Language Proficiency” and the “SPOT Test.

text:
【第1頁】
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
Ryukoku University Guide for 
Exchange Students 
Please read this guide VERY carefully before filling in the 
application form. We will explain and help you with your 
application preparation. As immigration procedures take a very 
long time for processing, please be sure to submit ALL required 
materials as early as possible. 


【第2頁】
2 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Please complete your application process while following the procedures below. 
 
Qualifications for Application 
Only students who are enrolled at universities which have a Student Exchange Agreement with Ryukoku University, 
and who have been nominated by their home university, are eligible to apply. 
 
Application Procedures 
The Home University Coordinator must complete the online form titled <2027 年度交換留学ノミネーシ
ョン／Spring 2027 Exchange Program Nomination Form>. 
Nomination Period: October 6th ~ November 9th, 2026 23:59 (Japan Time) 
 
The Nominated Students must receive a link from the Home University Coordinator for the online form titled 
<Exchange Application Spring 2027 Entry> and complete the form within the following period: 
Application Period: October 6th ~ November 9th, 2026 23:59 (Japan Time) 
 
① Notification of Acceptance or Non-Acceptance 
Those who have completed the above procedures by the deadline will be notified of their acceptance or non-
acceptance in approximately the middle of December. 
 
② Issuance of the Official Acceptance Letter and COE (Certificate of Eligibility) 
These documents will be sent to accepted students at approximately the beginning of February. 
 
 
 
 
 
To receive a student visa from the Japanese Embassy or Consulate, you need a Certificate of Eligibility (COE). The 
Ryukoku University Center for the Promotion of Global Education (R-Globe) Office will apply for this (in Japan) 
on your behalf, after we rece ive all your required application documents. It generally takes six to eight weeks for 
the Certificate to be issued, so be sure to submit all your materials as soon as possible to avoid any possible delay. 
Once we receive the Certificate of Eligibility, we  will send it together with the Letter of Acceptance to you in a 
“Welcome Package”, addressed to your home university. Once you receive these documents, please take the 
Certificate of Eligibility and the Letter of Acceptance to the Japanese Embassy in your own country to apply for 
your student visa. 
 
 
 
Certificate of Eligibility & Student Visa 
Spring 2027 Exchange Program Application Procedures 

【第3頁】

Exchange students will primarily pursue their studies through the Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP), which 
will be launched in April 2026. The JSP curriculum is built upon the university's guiding principle of "Magokoro" 
(sincerity, compassion, and altruism). It offers a combination of three subject groups: Japanese language study, 
international collaborative courses that involve Project-Based Learning (PBL) with domestic and other international 
students, and subjects focused on Japanese society, culture, and industry. 
 
In addition to courses offered in Japanese and elective subjects, JSP also offers many subjects taught in English. 
This allows a wide range of students to enroll, from Japanese  language beginners to advanced learners aiming to 
take the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT). This program is designed to provide significant academic and 
personal growth through field trips, cultural activities, and interaction with the local community.  Furthermore, 
students who meet certain conditions may also be permitted to enroll in courses offered by Ryukoku University’s  
undergraduate and graduate schools (All Exchange Students may register for regular subjects which are offered in 
English. Only students assigned to JSP IV・JSP V may register for regular subjects which are offered in Japanese). 
Overall, during their exchange term, students are required to register for 15 or more credits per semester. 
 
 
 
 
 
●There are three courses of study for exchange students, as follows: 
① Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP) 
This program aims to provide an opportunity for international students and local Ryukoku University students to 
learn together, deepen their understanding of different cultures and values, and develop practical communication 
skills. S tudents from diverse backgrounds collaborate in their classes through discussions, group work, and 
fieldwork. Subjects are offered in both Japanese and English. In addition, it is possible to complete the program 
entirely in English so students who have never studied Japanese are able to participate. 
If a student wishes to register for subjects conducted in Japanese, they must be assessed as having the necessary 
level of Japanese proficiency (based on the results of the Placement Test). If the student’s Japanese proficiency is 
not sufficient, they will take classes conducted in English.

Furthermore, students assigned to classes JSP-1 ~ JSP-III may register for undergraduate-level and graduate-level 
subjects offered in English. Students assigned to classes  JSP-IV and JSP-V are eligible to register for all 
undergraduate-level and graduate-level subjects. 
② Registration for Regular Undergraduate Faculty Classes Only                                              
 
This option applies to Exchange Students who, based on the conditions set forth in the Student Exchange Agreement 
concluded between specific Faculties at both universities, may only register for classes in the Faculty to which they 
belong. (Ryukoku University Faculty of Economics and Dalian University of Foreign Languages School of Japanese 
Studies） 
 
③ Registration for Regular Graduate School Classes Only                                          
 
This option applies to Exchange Students who, based on the conditions set forth in a Student Exchange Agreement 
concluded between specific Graduate Schools at both universities, may only  register for classes in the Graduate 
School to which they belong. (Agreements concluded with our Graduate School of Advanced Science and 
Technology). 
 
 
 
 
●First, the student should confirm with the Study Abroad Coordinator at their home university regarding whether 
exchange student is possible under the existing Student Exchange Agreement. In some cases, due to agreements 
concluded between specific Faculties or Graduate Schools, the student may be limited to registering for subjects 
only within a specific major.  
● If the student selects the English Track, they will not be able to register for subjects conducted in Japanese.  
If you indicate this selection (JSP-I) in your application, you will be placed in a Japanese language class at the  
JSP-I level. In principle, it is not possible to change to JSP-II or a higher-level class after submitting your application, 
so please consider your choice carefully before applying.  However, exchange students with a one-year exchange 
term may, if they wish, take a Japanese language placement test after the end of their first semester.  If the se 
placement test results indicate that the student possesses Japanese language proficiency equivalent to JSP -II or 
above, they may be assigned to JSP-II or another appropriate higher-level class in their second semester. 
Please note that the final class placement will be determined by Ryukoku University based on the placement test 
results and the student's overall Japanese language proficiency. 
●For the Japanese track, it is recommended that the student has completed at least 300 hours of Japanese language 
study or has Japanese proficiency equivalent to JLPT N4 or higher.  
●Based on the results of the Japanese placement test, if the student’s Japanese level is determined to be lower than 
that required for entry into JSP-II, they may be reassigned to JSP-I (English Track)

needs and language ability. 
● Japanese language subjects are be organized into classes based on proficiency level.

To complete the JSP program, students must earn credits from the JSP courses listed below. 
Students who meet the completion requirements will be awarded a JSP Certificate of Completion (Digital Badge). 
- For students enrolled for one semester: Completion of 15 or more JSP course credits 
- For students enrolled for two semesters: Completion of 30 or more JSP course credits 
 
 
 
 
 
●You are required to register for a minimum of 15 JSP credits per semester (30 JSP credits per year). (Please note 
that this minimum registered credit requirement is subject to change.) Be sure to confirm with the responsible 
staff or faculty member at your home university regarding which fields of study you must complete studies in at

Ryukoku University has three campuses in and around Kyoto. These campuses are close to train lines and within 
easy reach of each other, so you should be able to commute easily between them.  
*There are free shuttle buses between the campuses throughout the day, with Fukakusa as the central campus. (From 
Fukakusa to Omiya: 20 Minutes; From Fukakusa to Seta: 40 minutes).  
 
 
◆京都深草キャンパス 
KYOTO FUKAKUSA Campus, located in southern Kyoto, is the central 
campus.  The Center for the Promotion of Global Education and all 
lectures in the JSP Program are based here. The Faculties of International 
Studies, Economics, Business Administration, Law, Policy Science, and 
Sociology, along with first- and second-year subjects of the Faculty of 
Letters and the Faculty of Psychology are located here. 
 
◆京都大宮キャンパス 
KYOTO OMIY A Campus is our original campus (founded in 1639), and is 
located in central Kyoto, just beside historic Nishi Hongwanji Temple. Third 
and Fourth Year subjects of the Faculty of Letters and the Faculty of 
Psychology, as well as those of the Graduate Sc hool of Psychology, are 
taught here, and the campus provides an ideal calm and relaxed atmosphere 
for study and research. 
 
◆大津びわ湖キャンパス 
OTSU BIW AKO Campus, located in Shiga Prefecture’s “Biwako Culture 
Park”, is surrounded by nature and is the newest and largest campus, The 
Faculties of Science and Technology, Agriculture , Environmental 
Sustainability, and Informatics are located here.
